docs.text:
find . -type f -name 'settings*.py' -print

Projects may use:

settings.py

settings/
├── base.py
├── development.py
├── staging.py
└── production.py

Review the configuration actually used in production.

docs.title: High-Value settings.py Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'DEBUG|SECRET_KEY|ALLOWED_HOSTS|CSRF_|SESSION_|SECURE_|CORS_|DATABASES|MIDDLEWARE|INSTALLED_APPS|AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS|AUTH_USER_MODEL|REST_FRAMEWORK' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: DEBUG
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'DEBUG\s*=' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Potentially unsafe production configuration:

DEBUG = True

Django debug output can expose substantial internal application information.

However:

DEBUG = True in development settings
    !=
Production vulnerability

Determine which settings module is deployed.

docs.title: SECRET_KEY
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'SECRET_KEY\s*=' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Candidate:

SECRET_KEY = "hard-coded-production-secret"

Prefer loading sensitive production values from appropriately protected configuration or secret-management systems.

Do not automatically report example or test keys as production secrets.

docs.title: Search Environment Loading
docs.text:
rg -n \
'os\.environ|os\.getenv|environ\.Env|decouple|dotenv|SECRET_KEY' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: ALLOWED_HOSTS
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'ALLOWED_HOSTS\s*=' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Example:

ALLOWED_HOSTS = [
    "app.example.com",
]

Review broad configurations such as:

ALLOWED_HOSTS = ["*"]

but do not classify them as exploitable without understanding:

Reverse proxy validation
Host usage
Absolute URL generation
Password-reset workflows
Deployment architecture

Django's host validation is an important control against malicious Host values.

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text:
Locate:

rg -n \
'MIDDLEWARE\s*=' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Typical security-relevant middleware includes:

SecurityMiddleware
SessionMiddleware
CommonMiddleware
CsrfViewMiddleware
AuthenticationMiddleware

Review whether expected middleware has been removed or replaced.

docs.title: Installed Applications
docs.text:
rg -n \
'INSTALLED_APPS\s*=' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Look for:

django.contrib.admin
django.contrib.auth
rest_framework
corsheaders
debug_toolbar
silk
django_extensions
third-party authentication packages

Development/debug packages deserve additional attention if enabled in production.

docs.title: Route Discovery
docs.text:
Django routes are normally defined using:

path()
re_path()
include()

Search:

rg -n \
'urlpatterns|path\(|re_path\(|include\(' \
--glob 'urls.py' \
.

Broader search:

rg -n \
'\b(path|re_path|include)\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Basic Route
docs.text:
Example:

urlpatterns = [
    path(
        "users/<int:user_id>/",
        views.user_detail,
        name="user-detail",
    ),
]

Map:

/users/<user_id>/
        |
        v
views.user_detail

docs.title: Included Routes
docs.text:
Example:

path(
    "api/",
    include("api.urls"),
)

Follow every include().

Conceptually:

project/urls.py
      |
      +-- accounts.urls
      |
      +-- api.urls
      |
      +-- admin.site.urls

docs.title: Route Inventory
docs.text:
Create:

Method Route View Authentication Authorisation GET /profile/ profile() Login Self GET /users/<id>/ user_detail() Login ? POST /upload/ upload() Login User DELETE /api/users/<id>/ UserViewSet Token Admin

This route map becomes the foundation of the review.

docs.title: Function-Based Views
docs.text:
Example:

def profile(request):
    ...

Search:

rg -n \
'^def [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\(request' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Async views:

rg -n \
'^async def [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\(request' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Class-Based Views
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'class .*View\(|class .*APIView\(|class .*ViewSet\(|class .*GenericAPIView\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Common Django classes include:

View
TemplateView
DetailView
ListView
CreateView
UpdateView
DeleteView
FormView

DRF adds:

APIView
GenericAPIView
ViewSet
ModelViewSet
ReadOnlyModelViewSet

docs.title: HTTP Method Handlers
docs.text:
Class-based views commonly use:

def get(self, request):
    ...

def post(self, request):
    ...

Search:

rg -n \
'def (get|post|put|patch|delete|head|options)\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: User-Controlled Input
docs.text:
Common Django input sources include:

request.GET
request.POST
request.FILES
request.COOKIES
request.headers
request.META
request.body

Route parameters are also attacker-controlled.

Example:

def invoice(request, invoice_id):
    ...

invoice_id originates from the URL.

docs.title: Input Source Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'request\.(GET|POST|FILES|COOKIES|headers|META|body)' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: request.GET
docs.text:
Example:

search = request.GET.get("search")

Search:

rg -n \
'request\.GET' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: request.POST
docs.text:
rg -n \
'request\.POST' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Uploaded Files
docs.text:
rg -n \
'request\.FILES|UploadedFile|FileField|ImageField' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Headers
docs.text:
rg -n \
'request\.headers|request\.META' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Potential attacker-controlled metadata includes:

Host
Origin
Referer
User-Agent
X-Forwarded-For
X-Forwarded-Host
X-Forwarded-Proto
Custom headers

Trust depends on deployment architecture.

docs.title: JSON Input
docs.text:
Traditional Django views may parse:

json.loads(request.body)

Search:

rg -n \
'json\.loads\(request\.body|request\.body' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Django REST Framework normally provides:

request.data

Search:

rg -n \
'request\.data' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Django's authentication system commonly exposes:

request.user

Search:

rg -n \
'request\.user|authenticate\(|login\(|logout\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: login_required
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'@login_required' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Example:

@login_required
def profile(request):
    ...

This verifies that the user is authenticated.

It does not automatically provide:

Role authorisation
Object ownership
Tenant isolation
Business-level permission

docs.title: LoginRequiredMixin
docs.text:
Class-based views may use:

class ProfileView(
    LoginRequiredMixin,
    TemplateView
):
    ...

Search:

rg -n \
'LoginRequiredMixin' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: permission_required
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'@permission_required|PermissionRequiredMixin' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Example:

@permission_required(
    "accounts.delete_user",
    raise_exception=True,
)
def delete_user(request, user_id):
    ...

Review:

Correct permission?
Correct object?
Correct failure behaviour?

docs.title: user_passes_test
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'user_passes_test' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Example:

@user_passes_test(
    lambda user: user.is_staff
)
def admin_report(request):
    ...

Review the test itself.

docs.title: is_staff and is_superuser
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'is_staff|is_superuser' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Do not assume these checks are incorrect.

Determine whether they match the application's intended privilege model.

docs.title: Authentication Bypass Review
docs.text:
Compare routes that perform similar actions.

Example:

GET /account/
    -> @login_required

POST /account/update/
    -> @login_required

POST /account/delete/
    -> no authentication decorator

The missing control may be more important than a dangerous function.

docs.title: Authorisation
docs.text:
Authentication answers:

Who are you?

Authorisation answers:

Are you allowed to perform this action?

Search:

rg -n -i \
'permission|authorize|authorise|role|is_staff|is_superuser|owner|created_by|tenant|organization|organisation' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Object-Level Authorisation
docs.text:
A common Django vulnerability occurs when a view retrieves an object using an attacker-controlled ID without checking ownership.

Candidate:

@login_required
def invoice(request, invoice_id):
    invoice = Invoice.objects.get(
        id=invoice_id
    )

    return render(
        request,
        "invoice.html",
        {"invoice": invoice},
    )

Data flow:

/invoices/<invoice_id>/
          |
          v
invoice_id
          |
          v
Invoice.objects.get()
          |
          v
Invoice returned

Critical question:

Where is object-level authorisation?

docs.title: Safer Query Scoping
docs.text:
A stronger design may scope the lookup:

invoice = get_object_or_404(
    Invoice,
    id=invoice_id,
    owner=request.user,
)

Conceptually:

Object ID
   +
Authenticated User
   |
   v
Scoped Query

For multi-tenant applications:

invoice = get_object_or_404(
    Invoice,
    id=invoice_id,
    tenant=request.user.tenant,
)

The exact rule depends on the application's authorisation model.

docs.title: get_object_or_404
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'get_object_or_404\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Do not assume it provides authorisation.

Example:

get_object_or_404(
    Invoice,
    id=invoice_id,
)

only proves that the object exists.

It does not prove the current user may access it.

docs.title: ORM Object Lookup Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\.objects\.(get|filter|exclude|all|first|last|create|update|get_or_create|update_or_create)\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Prioritise lookups involving:

id
pk
user_id
account_id
invoice_id
document_id
tenant_id
organisation_id
organization_id

docs.title: Tenant Isolation
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'tenant|tenant_id|organisation|organization|workspace|account_id|company_id' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Map:

Authenticated User
       |
       v
Tenant Membership
       |
       v
Tenant-Scoped Queryset
       |
       v
Object

Look for code such as:

Document.objects.get(
    id=document_id
)

where expected scoping should resemble:

Document.objects.get(
    id=document_id,
    tenant=request.user.tenant,
)

docs.title: Django REST Framework
docs.text:
Django REST Framework is extremely common in Django applications.

Identify it:

rg -n \
'rest_framework|APIView|ViewSet|ModelViewSet|Serializer|ModelSerializer' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Important review areas include:

Authentication classes
Permission classes
Object permissions
Queryset filtering
Serializers
Mass assignment
Throttling
Parsers
Renderers
Custom actions

docs.title: DRF Authentication
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'authentication_classes|DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Authentication establishes identity.

It does not by itself determine whether an operation is authorised.

docs.title: DRF Permissions
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'permission_classes|DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES|AllowAny|IsAuthenticated|IsAdminUser|IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Example:

class AccountView(
    APIView
):
    permission_classes = [
        IsAuthenticated
    ]

This ensures authentication.

It does not necessarily ensure object ownership.

docs.title: AllowAny
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'AllowAny|permission_classes\s*=\s*\[\s*\]' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

AllowAny may be completely appropriate for:

Login
Registration
Public content
Health endpoints
Webhook endpoints with independent authentication

Review the endpoint's intended security requirements.

docs.title: DRF Default Permissions
docs.text:
Review:

REST_FRAMEWORK = {
    "DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES": [
        ...
    ],
}

Search:

rg -n \
'REST_FRAMEWORK|DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

DRF's default permission policy is unrestricted unless the application configures a different default. Therefore, explicit application policy is important when reviewing APIs.

docs.title: DRF Object-Level Permissions
docs.text:
Custom permission:

class IsOwner(
    permissions.BasePermission
):
    def has_object_permission(
        self,
        request,
        view,
        obj,
    ):
        return obj.owner == request.user

Search:

rg -n \
'has_object_permission|check_object_permissions' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

DRF generic views call object-level permission checks during normal object retrieval, but custom object retrieval logic may need to call check_object_permissions() explicitly. List endpoints also require queryset filtering because object-level permission checks are not automatically applied to every returned object.

docs.title: Dangerous Custom get_object()
docs.text:
Candidate:

def get_object(self):
    return Invoice.objects.get(
        pk=self.kwargs["pk"]
    )

Review whether this bypasses expected object permission checks.

Safer custom implementations may need:

obj = get_object_or_404(
    self.get_queryset(),
    pk=self.kwargs["pk"],
)

self.check_object_permissions(
    self.request,
    obj,
)

return obj

The exact implementation depends on the view architecture.

docs.title: DRF get_queryset()
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'def get_queryset\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Example:

def get_queryset(self):
    return Invoice.objects.filter(
        owner=self.request.user
    )

This can enforce visibility at the queryset level.

Review every override.

docs.title: Dangerous Broad Queryset
docs.text:
Candidate:

queryset = Invoice.objects.all()

This is not automatically vulnerable.

Ask:

Are permission classes present?
Is get_queryset() overridden?
Are object permissions applied?
Should list responses be tenant-scoped?

docs.title: DRF Serializers
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'class .*Serializer|ModelSerializer|Serializer\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Serializers are security-relevant because they control:

Accepted input
Validation
Writable fields
Read-only fields
Object creation
Object updates
Output

DRF serializers deserialize and validate incoming data before exposing it as validated_data.

docs.title: ModelSerializer
docs.text:
Example:

class UserSerializer(
    serializers.ModelSerializer
):
    class Meta:
        model = User
        fields = [
            "username",
            "email",
        ]

Explicit field lists are easier to reason about during security review.

docs.title: Serializer fields
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'fields\s*=|exclude\s*=|read_only_fields|write_only|read_only' \
--glob 'serializers.py' \
.

Security-sensitive fields include:

is_staff
is_superuser
role
permissions
groups
owner
owner_id
tenant
tenant_id
balance
verified
status
approved

docs.title: read_only_fields
docs.text:
Example:

class UserSerializer(
    serializers.ModelSerializer
):
    class Meta:
        model = User
        fields = [
            "username",
            "email",
            "is_staff",
        ]

        read_only_fields = [
            "is_staff",
        ]

DRF read-only fields appear in output but are not accepted as writable input.

docs.title: Serializer Validation
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'def validate_|def validate\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Example:

def validate_role(self, value):
    ...

and:

def validate(self, attrs):
    ...

Review whether validation implements:

Security rules
Cross-field constraints
Tenant restrictions
State transitions
Ownership rules

Validation is not a substitute for authorisation.

docs.title: Serializer create() and update()
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'def create\(self, validated_data|def update\(self, instance, validated_data' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

These are high-value locations for mass assignment and privilege changes.

docs.title: Mass Assignment
docs.text:
Candidate:

def update(
    self,
    instance,
    validated_data,
):
    for key, value in validated_data.items():
        setattr(
            instance,
            key,
            value,
        )

    instance.save()

    return instance

Whether this is dangerous depends on which fields can enter validated_data.

Trace:

Request Data
    |
    v
Serializer Fields
    |
    v
Validation
    |
    v
validated_data
    |
    v
Model Update

Refer to:

Mass Assignment

docs.title: DRF Custom Actions
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'@action\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Example:

@action(
    detail=True,
    methods=["post"],
)
def approve(
    self,
    request,
    pk=None,
):
    ...

Custom actions frequently implement security-sensitive business operations.

Review:

Authentication
Permission classes
Object permissions
State transition
Ownership
Role requirements

docs.title: Forms
docs.text:
Django forms provide structured validation.

Search:

rg -n \
'class .*Form\(|class .*ModelForm\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Example:

class ProfileForm(
    forms.ModelForm
):
    class Meta:
        model = Profile
        fields = [
            "display_name",
            "bio",
        ]

docs.title: ModelForm Mass Assignment
docs.text:
Review:

fields = "__all__"

Search:

rg -n \
'fields\s*=\s*["'\'']__all__["'\'']' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

This is not automatically vulnerable.

Determine whether the underlying model contains security-sensitive fields that users should not modify.

docs.title: Form Validation
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'def clean\(|def clean_[A-Za-z_]' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Example:

def clean_email(self):
    ...

Review:

Validation correctness
Canonicalisation
Cross-field rules
Business constraints

docs.title: SQL Injection
docs.text:
Django's ORM normally constructs parameterised database queries.

Typical ORM usage:

User.objects.filter(
    username=username
)

does not involve manually concatenating SQL.

The highest-value areas are raw SQL interfaces.

docs.title: raw()
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\.raw\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Candidate:

query = (
    "SELECT * FROM accounts_user "
    "WHERE username = '"
    + username
    + "'"
)

User.objects.raw(query)

Trace attacker-controlled values into the SQL string.

docs.title: RawSQL
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'RawSQL\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Raw SQL constructs require manual review because the developer controls the SQL. Django's security documentation specifically notes that raw SQL mechanisms require safe handling of user input.

docs.title: connection.cursor()
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'connection\.cursor\(|cursor\.execute\(|cursor\.executemany\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Candidate:

with connection.cursor() as cursor:
    cursor.execute(
        f"""
        SELECT *
        FROM accounts_user
        WHERE username = '{username}'
        """
    )

docs.title: Parameterised Raw Query
docs.text:
Preferred pattern:

with connection.cursor() as cursor:
    cursor.execute(
        """
        SELECT *
        FROM accounts_user
        WHERE username = %s
        """,
        [username],
    )

Do not manually quote placeholders.

docs.title: extra()
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\.extra\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

extra() is an older raw-SQL-style queryset API and deserves review when encountered.

Do not report it solely because it exists.

Trace how SQL fragments and parameters are constructed.

docs.title: SQL Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\.raw\(|RawSQL\(|connection\.cursor\(|cursor\.execute\(|cursor\.executemany\(|\.extra\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Refer to:

SQL Injection

docs.title: Dynamic ORM Fields
docs.text:
ORM parameterisation does not make arbitrary attacker-controlled query structure safe.

Candidate:

sort = request.GET.get("sort")

results = User.objects.order_by(
    sort
)

This may not be SQL injection in the classic sense, but dynamic field selection still deserves review.

Prefer server-controlled mappings where appropriate:

allowed_sort = {
    "name": "username",
    "date": "date_joined",
}

sort_field = allowed_sort.get(
    sort,
    "username",
)

docs.title: Queryset Filters from Dictionaries
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\.filter\(\*\*|\.get\(\*\*|\.exclude\(\*\*' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Candidate:

filters = request.data

User.objects.filter(
    **filters
)

Review whether users can influence:

Unexpected fields
Relationship traversal
Tenant scoping
Business logic

Do not automatically classify this as SQL injection.

docs.title: XSS
docs.text:
Django templates escape variables by default in normal HTML template contexts.

Example:

<p>{{ username }}</p>

The major review targets are mechanisms that intentionally bypass escaping.

docs.title: mark_safe
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'mark_safe\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Candidate:

return mark_safe(
    request.GET.get("message")
)

Trace whether attacker-controlled data is explicitly marked safe.

docs.title: safe Filter
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\|\s*safe\b' \
--glob '*.html' \
--glob '*.htm' \
--glob '*.txt' \
.

Candidate:

{{ biography|safe }}

Trace where biography originates.

docs.title: autoescape off
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'autoescape\s+off' \
--glob '*.html' \
.

Example:

{% autoescape off %}
    {{ content }}
{% endautoescape %}

Review all variables inside the block.

docs.title: format_html
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'format_html\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

format_html() is designed to build HTML while escaping interpolated arguments.

Do not classify its use as XSS solely because HTML is being generated.

Review any arguments already marked safe.

docs.title: format_html_join
docs.text:
rg -n \
'format_html_join\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Again, investigate data flow rather than flagging the API itself.

docs.title: html_safe
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'html_safe|SafeString|SafeData' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

These are high-value review locations because they interact with Django's escaping model.

docs.title: Template Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'mark_safe\(|format_html\(|format_html_join\(|SafeString|\|\s*safe\b|autoescape\s+off' \
--glob '*.py' \
--glob '*.html' \
.

Refer to:

Cross-Site Scripting

HTML Injection

docs.title: JavaScript Context
docs.text:
Even escaped template values can become dangerous when placed into inappropriate contexts.

Candidate:

<script>
    const username = "{{ username }}";
</script>

HTML escaping and JavaScript-string escaping are different security contexts.

Review template data inserted into:

JavaScript
CSS
URLs
HTML attributes
Inline event handlers

docs.title: json_script
docs.text:
For safely transferring structured data into JavaScript, Django provides mechanisms such as json_script.

Search:

rg -n \
'json_script' \
--glob '*.html' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review how the resulting data is subsequently consumed in JavaScript.

docs.title: Server-Side Template Injection
docs.text:
Traditional Django template rendering normally uses server-controlled template names:

return render(
    request,
    "profile.html",
    context,
)

The review priority increases if attacker input controls template source or template selection.

Search:

rg -n \
'Template\(|Engine\(|from_string\(|get_template\(|select_template\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Candidate:

template_source = request.POST["template"]

template = Template(
    template_source
)

return HttpResponse(
    template.render(context)
)

Review the actual template engine and capabilities before determining impact.

Refer to:

Server-Side Template Injection

docs.title: Template Path Control
docs.text:
Candidate:

template_name = request.GET["template"]

return render(
    request,
    template_name,
)

Review whether attacker-controlled template names can expose unintended templates or interact with custom template loaders.

docs.title: CSRF
docs.text:
Django provides CSRF protection through middleware and template mechanisms.

Review middleware:

rg -n \
'CsrfViewMiddleware' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: csrf_exempt
docs.text:
High-value search:

rg -n \
'@csrf_exempt|csrf_exempt\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Example:

@csrf_exempt
def update_profile(request):
    ...

Do not automatically report every exemption.

Determine:

Does the endpoint change state?
Does it use cookie-based authentication?
Is there another request-authentication mechanism?
Is the endpoint intentionally called cross-site?

docs.title: csrf_protect
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'@csrf_protect|csrf_protect\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Template CSRF Tokens
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'csrf_token' \
--glob '*.html' \
.

Example:

<form method="post">
    {% csrf_token %}
</form>

docs.title: CSRF Trusted Origins
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS|CSRF_COOKIE_|CSRF_USE_SESSIONS' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review broad trusted-origin configurations.

Refer to:

Cross-Site Request Forgery

docs.title: CORS
docs.text:
Django applications commonly use:

django-cors-headers

Search:

rg -n -i \
'corsheaders|CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS|CORS_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS|CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS|CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN_REGEXES' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Broad CORS
docs.text:
Candidate:

CORS_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS = True

This is not automatically exploitable.

Determine:

Are credentials permitted?
What endpoints return sensitive information?
What authentication mechanism is used?
Can an attacker-controlled origin read sensitive responses?

Refer to:

Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)

docs.title: Open Redirect
docs.text:
Django redirect functionality includes:

redirect()
HttpResponseRedirect()
HttpResponsePermanentRedirect()

Search:

rg -n \
'redirect\(|HttpResponseRedirect\(|HttpResponsePermanentRedirect\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Candidate:

next_url = request.GET.get("next")

return redirect(next_url)

Trace whether external destinations are allowed.

docs.title: Login Redirects
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'next|redirect_to|LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL|LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URL' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Login flows frequently accept a destination such as:

?next=/dashboard/

Review whether external destinations are properly rejected.

docs.title: URL Safety Helpers
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

This Django helper can be used when validating redirect targets against expected hosts and schemes.

Review the arguments and trusted-host set.

Refer to:

Open Redirect

docs.title: SSRF
docs.text:
Django itself does not prevent application code from making unsafe outbound requests.

Search:

rg -n \
'requests\.(get|post|put|patch|delete|request)\(|httpx\.|urlopen\(|aiohttp\.ClientSession' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Candidate:

url = request.POST["url"]

response = requests.get(
    url
)

Data flow:

request.POST["url"]
        |
        v
url
        |
        v
requests.get()
        |
        v
Outbound Request

Review:

Destination allowlist
Scheme
Hostname
Port
DNS resolution
Redirects
IPv4/IPv6
Internal networks
Loopback
Link-local
Cloud metadata
Egress controls

Refer to:

Server Side Request Forgery

docs.title: Path Traversal
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\bopen\(|Path\(|os\.path\.join\(|FileResponse\(|StreamingHttpResponse\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Candidate:

filename = request.GET["file"]

path = os.path.join(
    settings.MEDIA_ROOT,
    filename,
)

return FileResponse(
    open(path, "rb")
)

Do not assume os.path.join() provides containment.

Trace the final canonical path.

docs.title: FileResponse
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'FileResponse\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review where the opened file path originates.

docs.title: MEDIA_ROOT
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'MEDIA_ROOT|MEDIA_URL|STATIC_ROOT|STATIC_URL' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review separation between:

Uploaded content
Static content
Application source
Templates
Sensitive files

Refer to:

Path Traversal

docs.title: File Upload
docs.text:
Django provides:

request.FILES

and model fields such as:

FileField
ImageField

Search:

rg -n \
'request\.FILES|FileField\(|ImageField\(|UploadedFile|FileSystemStorage' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Upload Review
docs.text:
For each upload flow determine:

Who can upload?
What file types are expected?
How is filename handled?
Where is the file stored?
Can the file overwrite another file?
Is it publicly accessible?
Is content served with a safe Content-Type?
Is active content possible?
Is the file processed?
Is it passed to another parser?
Is it extracted?
Is it converted?

docs.title: File Extensions
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'extension|content_type|mimetype|mime|filename' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Do not assume extension validation alone proves content safety.

docs.title: File Validators
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'FileExtensionValidator|validate_image_file_extension|validators=' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review whether validation matches the actual downstream risk.

docs.title: upload_to
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'upload_to\s*=' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Example:

file = models.FileField(
    upload_to="documents/",
)

Custom upload path functions deserve additional review.

docs.title: Custom Upload Path
docs.text:
Example:

def upload_path(
    instance,
    filename,
):
    return (
        f"{instance.user.username}/"
        f"{filename}"
    )

Review attacker control over:

filename
username
directory components

docs.title: Archive Processing
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'zipfile|ZipFile|tarfile|TarFile|extractall\(|unpack_archive\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Uploaded archives can create:

Path traversal
Resource exhaustion
Unexpected file overwrite
Unsafe downstream processing

Refer to:

File Upload Security

docs.title: Insecure Deserialization
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'pickle\.(load|loads)\(|dill\.(load|loads)\(|cloudpickle|joblib\.load|yaml\.(load|unsafe_load)\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Candidate:

obj = pickle.loads(
    request.body
)

Never deserialize untrusted pickle data.

Refer to:

Insecure Deserialization

docs.title: Django Signed Data
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'django\.core\.signing|signing\.(dumps|loads)|Signer\(|TimestampSigner\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Signed data provides integrity when correctly implemented.

However, review:

SECRET_KEY security
Salt separation
Expiration
Purpose
What data is trusted after verification

A valid signature does not automatically mean the underlying action is authorised.

docs.title: Session Management
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'SESSION_ENGINE|SESSION_COOKIE_|SESSION_EXPIRE_AT_BROWSER_CLOSE|SESSION_COOKIE_AGE|request\.session' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Session Cookie Settings
docs.text:
High-value settings:

SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE
SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY
SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE
SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN
SESSION_COOKIE_PATH

Search:

rg -n \
'SESSION_COOKIE_(SECURE|HTTPONLY|SAMESITE|DOMAIN|PATH)' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Remember that settings can be overridden by environment-specific configuration.

docs.title: CSRF Cookie Settings
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'CSRF_COOKIE_(SECURE|HTTPONLY|SAMESITE|DOMAIN)' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Do not blindly apply session-cookie assumptions to CSRF cookies. Understand Django's CSRF design and the application's JavaScript requirements.

docs.title: Secure Proxy SSL Header
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Example:

SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER = (
    "HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO",
    "https",
)

This configuration is security-sensitive because it depends on the reverse proxy reliably controlling the corresponding header.

Review deployment architecture.

docs.title: USE_X_FORWARDED_HOST
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'USE_X_FORWARDED_HOST|USE_X_FORWARDED_PORT' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Incorrect trust in forwarded headers can contribute to:

Host confusion
Incorrect absolute URLs
Security-sensitive redirects
Password-reset poisoning
Logging inaccuracies

docs.title: Host Header Usage
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'request\.get_host\(|request\.build_absolute_uri\(|request\.META.*HTTP_HOST|request\.headers.*Host' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: build_absolute_uri
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'build_absolute_uri\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

High-value contexts:

Password-reset emails
Account activation
Email verification
OAuth callbacks
Generated external links

Determine whether the resulting host is derived from trusted configuration or request metadata.

Refer to:

HTTP Host Header Attacks

docs.title: Password Reset
docs.text:
Django provides built-in password-reset functionality.

Search:

rg -n -i \
'PasswordReset|PasswordResetView|PasswordResetForm|PasswordResetTokenGenerator|password_reset|reset_password' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review custom implementations carefully.

docs.title: Custom Reset Tokens
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'reset_token|password_reset_token|forgot_password|forgot.?password' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review:

Randomness
Expiration
Single use
User binding
Enumeration
Rate limiting
Host generation
Session invalidation

Refer to:

Password Reset Security

docs.title: Password Handling
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'set_password\(|check_password\(|make_password\(|check_password\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Django provides password hashing infrastructure.

Review custom password storage separately.

docs.title: Dangerous Direct Password Assignment
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\.password\s*=' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Candidate:

user.password = password
user.save()

This may store the value without Django's normal password hashing workflow.

Expected application code generally uses:

user.set_password(password)

Validate surrounding code before reporting.

docs.title: Password Hashers
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'PASSWORD_HASHERS' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review custom or legacy configurations.

docs.title: MFA
docs.text:
Django MFA may be implemented through third-party packages or custom code.

Search:

rg -n -i \
'totp|hotp|otp|mfa|2fa|two.?factor|recovery.?code|backup.?code' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review:

Enrollment
Secret generation
Verification
Replay
Rate limiting
Recovery
Reset
Remember-device functionality
Bypass paths

Refer to:

Multi-Factor Authentication Security

docs.title: OAuth / OIDC
docs.text:
Common Django integrations include:

django-allauth
social-auth-app-django
mozilla-django-oidc
Authlib integrations

Search:

rg -n -i \
'oauth|openid|oidc|allauth|social_auth|client_id|client_secret|redirect_uri|state|nonce|code_verifier' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review:

State validation
Nonce
PKCE
Issuer
Audience
Redirect URI
Account linking
Callback handling
Token storage

Refer to:

OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect Security

docs.title: SAML
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'saml|python3-saml|pysaml|xmlsec|onelogin' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review:

Signature validation
Assertion validation
Issuer
Audience
Destination
Recipient
Replay protection
Attribute mapping
Account linking

Refer to:

SAML Security

docs.title: LDAP
docs.text:
Django applications may authenticate against LDAP.

Search:

rg -n -i \
'ldap|django_auth_ldap|AUTH_LDAP' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review custom LDAP filters and search construction.

Candidate:

ldap_filter = (
    "(uid="
    + username
    + ")"
)

Refer to:

LDAP Injection

docs.title: Command Injection
docs.text:
Django applications can invoke operating-system commands just like other Python applications.

Search:

rg -n \
'os\.(system|popen)\(|subprocess\.(run|Popen|call|check_call|check_output)\(|shell\s*=\s*True' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Candidate:

host = request.POST["host"]

subprocess.run(
    f"ping -c 1 {host}",
    shell=True,
)

Prefer avoiding shell invocation and passing arguments separately where possible.

Refer to:

OS Command Injection

docs.title: Dynamic Code Execution
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\beval\(|\bexec\(|\bcompile\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Candidate:

expression = request.POST["expression"]

result = eval(expression)

Attacker-controlled input reaching eval() or exec() is a high-priority review target.

docs.title: XML / XXE
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'xml\.etree|ElementTree|lxml|etree|xml\.dom|minidom|sax|XMLParser' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review:

Parser
Version
DTD support
Entity resolution
Network access
Input trust

Do not classify XML parsing alone as XXE.

Refer to:

XML External Entity Injection

docs.title: Information Disclosure
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'DEBUG\s*=|traceback|logger\.exception|print_exc|HttpResponse\(.*exception|str\(.*exception' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review whether exceptions expose:

Stack traces
Source paths
Database errors
Secrets
Internal URLs
User information
Configuration

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'logger\.(debug|info|warning|error|critical|exception)\(|logging\.(debug|info|warning|error|critical|exception)\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Look for:

Passwords
JWTs
Session IDs
API keys
Reset tokens
MFA codes
Authorization headers
Sensitive request bodies

docs.title: SecurityMiddleware
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'SecurityMiddleware|SECURE_' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Security-related settings may include:

SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT
SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS
SECURE_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS
SECURE_HSTS_PRELOAD
SECURE_CONTENT_TYPE_NOSNIFF
SECURE_REFERRER_POLICY

Do not assume missing source configuration means the deployed application lacks the corresponding protection.

Reverse proxies and CDNs may provide some HTTP controls.

Validate actual responses.

Refer to:

HTTP Security Headers

docs.title: Clickjacking
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'X_FRAME_OPTIONS|xframe_options_exempt|xframe_options_deny|xframe_options_sameorigin' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

High-value target:

@xframe_options_exempt

Review why framing is allowed.

Refer to:

Clickjacking

docs.title: Cache Security
docs.text:
Django provides several caching mechanisms.

Search:

rg -n \
'cache\.|cache_page|vary_on_headers|vary_on_cookie|CACHE_MIDDLEWARE|CACHES\s*=' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review cache keys and variation for:

Authentication
User
Tenant
Role
Cookie
Host
Language
Headers
Query parameters

docs.title: cache_page
docs.text:
Example:

@cache_page(60 * 15)
def dashboard(request):
    ...

If the response is user-specific, determine whether the cache is appropriately separated.

Refer to:

Web Cache Poisoning

Web Cache Deception

docs.title: Business Logic
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'price|amount|balance|discount|coupon|refund|credit|quantity|approved|verified|status|role|permission|tenant' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review:

Pricing
Payments
Refunds
Credits
Discounts
Inventory
Approval workflows
Account state
Verification
Role changes
Tenant changes

docs.title: Model Methods
docs.text:
Security-sensitive business logic may reside in models.

Search:

rg -n \
'^class .*models\.Model|def save\(|def clean\(' \
--glob 'models.py' \
.

Do not review only views.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
Django signals can trigger hidden side effects.

Search:

rg -n \
'@receiver|post_save|pre_save|post_delete|pre_delete|m2m_changed' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Example flow:

HTTP Request
    |
    v
Model Save
    |
    v
post_save Signal
    |
    v
External Request

The dangerous sink may not appear in the view.

docs.title: Race Conditions
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'transaction\.atomic|select_for_update|F\(|get_or_create|update_or_create' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

High-value workflows include:

Balance changes
Coupon redemption
Inventory
One-time tokens
Password reset
Invitation acceptance
Approval

docs.title: select_for_update
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'select_for_update\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

This may indicate explicit row locking.

Its presence does not automatically prove the workflow is race-safe.

Review the complete transaction.

docs.title: transaction.atomic
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'transaction\.atomic' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Map:

Read
 |
 v
Check
 |
 v
Modify
 |
 v
Commit

Determine whether concurrent requests can violate business invariants.

Refer to:

Race Conditions

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
Traditional Django does not automatically provide comprehensive application-specific rate limiting for every sensitive workflow.

Applications may use:

DRF throttling
django-ratelimit
Reverse proxy controls
WAF
Redis-based custom controls

Search:

rg -n -i \
'ratelimit|rate_limit|throttle|DEFAULT_THROTTLE|throttle_classes' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: DRF Throttling
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES|DEFAULT_THROTTLE_RATES|throttle_classes' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Prioritise:

Login
Password reset
MFA
OTP
Registration
Verification
Expensive API calls
Exports

Do not conclude that rate limiting is absent from source alone because infrastructure may enforce it.

Refer to:

Rate Limiting and Anti-Automation

docs.title: Django Admin
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'admin\.site\.urls|admin\.site\.register|@admin\.register' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review:

Admin exposure
Custom admin actions
Object permissions
Sensitive fields
Bulk actions
File operations
Custom HTML

docs.title: Admin Actions
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'actions\s*=|@admin\.action' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Administrative interfaces are trusted functionality, but security boundaries still matter.

docs.title: ModelAdmin HTML
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'mark_safe\(|format_html\(' \
--glob 'admin.py' \
.

Admin interfaces can still contain stored XSS or unsafe HTML rendering.

docs.title: GraphQL
docs.text:
Django applications may use:

Graphene-Django
Strawberry
Ariadne

Search:

rg -n -i \
'graphene|strawberry|ariadne|graphql|resolver|mutation' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review:

Resolvers
Mutations
Authentication
Object-level authorisation
Field-level access
Query depth
Complexity
Batching
Introspection

Refer to:

GraphQL API Security

docs.title: WebSockets / Django Channels
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'channels|AsyncWebsocketConsumer|WebsocketConsumer|websocket|channel_layer' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Consumers
docs.text:
Example:

class ChatConsumer(
    AsyncWebsocketConsumer
):
    async def receive(
        self,
        text_data,
    ):
        ...

Search:

rg -n \
'WebsocketConsumer|AsyncWebsocketConsumer|def receive|async def receive' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review:

Connection authentication
Room/channel authorisation
Object access
Message authorisation
Origin validation
State-changing operations

Refer to:

WebSocket Security

docs.title: gRPC
docs.text:
Some Django systems communicate with gRPC services even when Django itself handles HTTP.

Search:

rg -n -i \
'grpc|Servicer|Stub\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review trust boundaries between:

Django HTTP Application
        |
        v
gRPC Client
        |
        v
Internal Service

Do not assume internal RPC calls are inherently trusted.

Refer to:

gRPC Security

docs.title: Background Jobs
docs.text:
Django commonly uses Celery.

Search:

rg -n -i \
'celery|shared_task|@.*\.task|\.delay\(|apply_async\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Second-Order Vulnerability Example
docs.text:
POST /integrations/
        |
        v
Webhook URL
        |
        v
Database
        |
        v
Celery Task
        |
        v
requests.post()
        |
        v
SSRF

Do not stop tracing when attacker-controlled data is stored.

docs.title: Celery Task Arguments
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'@shared_task|@.*\.task|\.delay\(|apply_async\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Review whether task arguments originate from users.

docs.title: Secrets Exposure
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'SECRET_KEY|password|passwd|secret|api[_-]?key|client[_-]?secret|access[_-]?key|private[_-]?key|token|DATABASE_URL' \
.

docs.title: Database Credentials
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'DATABASES\s*=|PASSWORD.*DATABASE|DATABASE_URL' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

Do not report placeholders or local development credentials as production secrets without evidence.

docs.title: Email Credentials
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'EMAIL_HOST_USER|EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Cloud Credentials
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n -i \
'AWS_ACCESS_KEY|AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY|AZURE_|GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS' \
.

Refer to:

Secrets Exposure

docs.title: Dependency Security
docs.text:
Find dependency files:

find . -maxdepth 3 -type f \( \
-name 'requirements*.txt' \
-o -name 'pyproject.toml' \
-o -name 'Pipfile*' \
-o -name 'poetry.lock' \
-o -name 'uv.lock' \
\) -print

Review:

Django version
DRF version
Authentication packages
CORS packages
Image parsers
XML libraries
Serialization libraries
Database drivers
Cloud SDKs

docs.title: pip-audit
docs.text:
pip-audit

Against a requirements file:

pip-audit \
-r requirements.txt

docs.title: OSV-Scanner
docs.text:
osv-scanner scan source -r .

A vulnerable dependency version is a candidate finding.

Determine:

Affected version?
Affected component used?
Vulnerable functionality reachable?
Attacker-controlled path?

Refer to:

Dependency Security

docs.title: Static Analysis
docs.text:
Useful tools include:

Semgrep
CodeQL
Bandit
pip-audit
OSV-Scanner
TruffleHog
Gitleaks

docs.title: Semgrep
docs.text:
semgrep scan \
--config auto \
.

Use Semgrep to identify:

Raw SQL
Command execution
Unsafe deserialization
Escaping bypasses
Hard-coded secrets
Dangerous request flows

Manual validation remains required.

docs.title: Bandit
docs.text:
bandit -r .

Exclude tests if appropriate:

bandit \
-r . \
-x ./tests

Bandit can help identify dangerous Python constructs, but Django-specific access-control and business-logic vulnerabilities still require manual review.

docs.title: CodeQL
docs.text:
CodeQL can assist with:

Data flow
Taint tracking
Call graphs
Variant analysis

It is particularly useful for tracing:

Request input
    |
    v
Multiple application layers
    |
    v
Dangerous sink

docs.title: Broad Django Security Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'request\.(GET|POST|FILES|COOKIES|headers|META|body|data)|@login_required|LoginRequiredMixin|permission_required|PermissionRequiredMixin|AllowAny|permission_classes|has_object_permission|get_queryset|\.objects\.(get|filter|all)\(|\.raw\(|RawSQL\(|connection\.cursor\(|cursor\.execute\(|mark_safe\(|\|\s*safe\b|autoescape\s+off|@csrf_exempt|redirect\(|HttpResponseRedirect\(|requests\.(get|post|request)\(|httpx\.|\bopen\(|FileResponse\(|pickle\.(load|loads)\(|yaml\.(load|unsafe_load)\(|os\.system\(|subprocess\.|shell\s*=\s*True|eval\(|exec\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
--glob '*.html' \
.

This is a candidate-discovery search.

It is not a vulnerability scanner.

docs.title: Route Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'urlpatterns|\bpath\(|\bre_path\(|include\(' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Authentication Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'@login_required|LoginRequiredMixin|authenticate\(|request\.user|permission_required|PermissionRequiredMixin|is_staff|is_superuser' \
--glob '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Reverse Sink Analysis
docs.text:
For large Django applications, begin with dangerous sinks.

Example:

Celery Task

      |
Integration Model
      ^
      |
POST /integrations/

High-value sinks:

.raw()
RawSQL()
cursor.execute()

os.system()
subprocess.*

eval()
exec()

pickle.loads()
yaml.load()

requests.*
httpx.*

open()
FileResponse()

mark_safe()
Template()

redirect()
HttpResponseRedirect()

docs.title: Finding Validation
docs.text:
Before reporting:

CODE MATCH
    |
    v
REACHABLE?
    |
    +-- No --> Usually discard / contextual note
    |
    v
ATTACKER CONTROLLED?
    |
    +-- No --> Continue contextual review
    |
    v
FRAMEWORK PROTECTION?
    |
    +-- Effective --> Protected
    |
    v
AUTHORISATION?
    |
    +-- Effective --> Protected
    |
    v
EXPLOITABLE?
    |
    +-- No --> Contextual / defence-in-depth
    |
    v
MEANINGFUL IMPACT?
    |
    +-- No --> Low significance
    |

CONFIRMED FINDING

docs.title: Example Finding - IDOR / BOLA
docs.text:
Title:
Missing Object-Level Authorisation on Document Endpoint

Route:
GET /documents/<document_id>/

Source:
URL parameter document_id

Data Flow:

document_id
    |
    v
Document.objects.get(id=document_id)
    |
    v
Document
    |
    v
render()

Authentication:
@login_required

Authorisation:
No ownership or tenant restriction was identified.

Impact:
An authenticated user may be able to access documents belonging to another user by modifying the document identifier.

Recommendation:
Scope the object query to resources the authenticated principal is authorised to access or perform an equivalent object-level permission check.

docs.title: Example Finding - Stored XSS
docs.text:
Title:
Stored Cross-Site Scripting Through Unsafe Template Rendering

Source:
Profile biography

Data Flow:

POST /profile/
      |
      v
Biography
      |
      v
Database
      |
      v
{{ biography|safe }}
      |
      v
Browser

Security Control:
Django's normal template escaping is explicitly bypassed by the safe filter.

Impact:
Attacker-controlled HTML may execute in the security context of users viewing the affected page, depending on the accepted content and browser context.

Recommendation:
Remove the safe filter for attacker-controlled content. If rich HTML is an application requirement, sanitise it using an appropriate allowlist-based HTML sanitisation strategy.

docs.title: Example Finding - SSRF
docs.text:
Title:
Server-Side Request Forgery in URL Preview Endpoint

Route:
POST /preview/

Source:
request.POST["url"]

Data Flow:

request.POST["url"]
        |
        v
url
        |
        v
requests.get(url)

Security Control:
No effective destination restriction was identified.

Impact:
The server may make outbound requests to destinations selected by the user, potentially including internal services depending on network connectivity.

Recommendation:
Prefer server-controlled destinations. If user-selected external URLs are required, implement strict destination validation and network-level egress restrictions.

docs.title: Example Finding - Raw SQL Injection
docs.text:
Title:
SQL Injection in User Search

Route:
GET /users/search/

Source:
request.GET["q"]

Data Flow:

request.GET["q"]
       |
       v
f-string SQL
       |
       v
connection.cursor()
       |
       v
cursor.execute()

Security Control:
No parameter binding was identified.

Recommendation:
Use the Django ORM where practical or pass attacker-controlled values as parameters to the database driver rather than constructing SQL syntax through string interpolation.

docs.title: Django ORM Means the Entire Application Is Safe from SQL Injection
docs.text:
Incorrect.

The ORM substantially reduces SQL injection risk when used normally, but applications can still use:

raw()
RawSQL()
cursor.execute()
extra()

and other custom query construction.

docs.title: login_required Means Authorisation Exists
docs.text:
Incorrect.

@login_required
       |
       v
Authenticated

does not prove:

Object ownership
Role permission
Tenant membership
Action permission

docs.title: get_object_or_404 Provides Authorisation
docs.text:
Incorrect.

get_object_or_404(
    Invoice,
    id=invoice_id,
)

checks existence.

It does not inherently prove that the user may access the object.

docs.title: IsAuthenticated Prevents IDOR
docs.text:
Incorrect.

permission_classes = [
    IsAuthenticated
]

means the user must be authenticated.

Object-level authorisation remains a separate concern.

docs.title: Serializer Validation Equals Authorisation
docs.text:
Incorrect.

A serializer may validate:

Type
Length
Format
Allowed values

while still allowing a user to modify an object they do not own.

docs.title: Every AllowAny Is Vulnerable
docs.text:
Incorrect.

Public endpoints legitimately exist.

Determine the intended security policy.

docs.title: Every csrf_exempt Is Vulnerable
docs.text:
Incorrect.

Determine:

Authentication mechanism
State change
Request context
Alternative verification

docs.title: Every mark_safe Is XSS
docs.text:
Incorrect.

Trace the value.

Static trusted string
    !=
Attacker-controlled HTML

docs.title: Every requests.get Is SSRF
docs.text:
Incorrect.

Determine who controls the URL and what destination restrictions exist.

docs.title: Every FileField Is an Upload Vulnerability
docs.text:
Incorrect.

Review the complete upload lifecycle.

docs.title: Every DEBUG=True Match Is a Production Vulnerability
docs.text:
Incorrect.

Determine which configuration is deployed.

docs.title: Every Broad Queryset Is IDOR
docs.text:
Incorrect.

Review:

Permissions
get_queryset()
Object permissions
Serializer behaviour
Endpoint type

docs.title: .NET / ASP.NET Core Source Code Review
docs.text:
This note provides a practical methodology for reviewing .NET and ASP.NET Core applications for security vulnerabilities.

The objective is not simply to search for dangerous .NET methods.

The objective is to trace attacker-controlled input through the application and determine whether it can reach security-sensitive operations without appropriate controls.

HTTP Request
     |
     v
ASP.NET Route
     |
     v
Controller / Minimal API
     |
     v
Model Binding
     |
     v
Validation
     |
     v
Authentication
     |
     v
Authorisation
     |
     v
Business Logic
     |
     v
Repository / Service
     |
     v
SECURITY-SENSITIVE SINK

Common technologies encountered during .NET source review include:

ASP.NET Core
ASP.NET MVC
ASP.NET Web API
Minimal APIs
Razor Pages
Blazor
Entity Framework Core
Entity Framework 6
ADO.NET
Dapper
SignalR
gRPC
WCF
System.Text.Json
Newtonsoft.Json

Authorised Security Testing

Review and test only applications and source code for which you have explicit authorisation. Source repositories can contain credentials, personal information, cryptographic material, internal infrastructure information and other sensitive data.

docs.title: Review Strategy
docs.text:
A practical .NET review can be approached as:

1. Identify solution and projects

2. Identify ASP.NET version and framework

3. Find application entry points

4. Enumerate routes

5. Map middleware

6. Map authentication

7. Map authorisation

8. Identify attacker-controlled sources

9. Identify validation

10. Identify dangerous sinks

11. Trace source-to-sink paths

12. Review business logic

13. Review configuration and secrets

14. Review dependencies

15. Review static-analysis findings

16. Perform variant analysis

17. Validate findings dynamically where authorised

docs.title: Identify the Application
docs.text:
Start by identifying .NET project files.

find . -type f \( \
-name '*.sln' \
-o -name '*.csproj' \
-o -name '*.fsproj' \
-o -name '*.vbproj' \
-o -name 'Directory.Build.props' \
-o -name 'Directory.Packages.props' \
-o -name 'packages.config' \
-o -name 'packages.lock.json' \
\) -print

Common files include:

Application.sln
Application.csproj
Directory.Build.props
Directory.Packages.props
packages.config
packages.lock.json

docs.title: Inspect Project Files
docs.text:
Inspect .csproj files.

cat Application.csproj

Look for:

<TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>

or:

<TargetFrameworks>net8.0;net9.0</TargetFrameworks>

Legacy applications may contain:

<TargetFrameworkVersion>v4.8</TargetFrameworkVersion>

The framework version affects:

Available APIs
Security defaults
Dependency support
Middleware architecture
Authentication configuration
Serialization behaviour

docs.title: Identify ASP.NET Core
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'Microsoft\.AspNetCore|WebApplication\.CreateBuilder|CreateHostBuilder|ConfigureServices|Configure\(' \
.

Common modern entry point:

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

builder.Services.AddControllers();

var app = builder.Build();

app.MapControllers();

app.Run();

Older ASP.NET Core applications commonly use:

Program.cs
Startup.cs

with:

public void ConfigureServices(IServiceCollection services)

and:

public void Configure(IApplicationBuilder app)

docs.title: Identify Legacy ASP.NET
docs.text:
Search for:

System.Web
Global.asax
Web.config
RouteConfig.cs
FilterConfig.cs
WebApiConfig.cs
App_Start

Command:

rg -n \
'System\.Web|HttpApplication|RouteConfig|WebApiConfig|RegisterRoutes|MapHttpRoute' \
.

Legacy ASP.NET applications require additional attention because their security configuration and APIs differ from ASP.NET Core.
