-g '*.html' \
.

Bypass APIs deserve review because they intentionally bypass Angular security handling.

docs.title: Vue
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'v-html' \
-g '*.vue' \
.

Review whether the value can contain attacker-controlled HTML.

docs.title: Open Redirect
docs.text:
rules:
  - id: javascript-navigation
    languages:
      - javascript
      - typescript
    message: Review attacker influence over navigation
    severity: WARNING

    pattern-either:
      - pattern: location.href = $URL
      - pattern: window.location = $URL
      - pattern: location.assign($URL)
      - pattern: location.replace($URL)
      - pattern: window.open($URL, ...)

docs.title: Authentication Review
docs.text:
OpenGrep can help locate authentication controls.

Look for:

Authentication middleware
Login handlers
Password verification
Session creation
JWT verification
OAuth callbacks
SAML handlers
MFA verification
Password reset flows

Do not expect generic static analysis to understand every custom authentication design automatically.

docs.title: Authorisation Review
docs.text:
Authorisation is one of the most important areas for manual review.

Model:

Route
  |
  v
Authentication
  |
  v
Object Identifier
  |
  v
Object Retrieval
  |
  v
Authorisation Check
  |
  v
Sensitive Operation

Static analysis can identify:

Object lookups
Permission functions
Authorisation annotations
Role checks
Tenant checks
Ownership checks

But the reviewer must understand the intended policy.

docs.title: Spring Security
docs.text:
Search:

SecurityFilterChain
authorizeHttpRequests
requestMatchers
permitAll
authenticated
hasRole
hasAuthority
@PreAuthorize
@PostAuthorize
@Secured

Example:

rules:
  - id: spring-permit-all
    languages:
      - java
    message: Review routes covered by permitAll
    severity: INFO

    pattern: $X.permitAll()

Do not report permitAll() itself as a vulnerability.

Determine which routes it affects.

docs.title: ASP.NET Core
docs.text:
Search:

[Authorize]
[AllowAnonymous]
RequireAuthorization
AddAuthorization
UseAuthentication
UseAuthorization
Policies
Roles
Claims

Candidate:

rules:
  - id: dotnet-allow-anonymous
    languages:
      - csharp
    message: Review anonymous endpoint exposure
    severity: INFO

    pattern: |
      [AllowAnonymous]
      $DECL

Rules may need adjustment for different declaration forms.

docs.title: Django
docs.text:
Review:

@login_required
permission_required
user_passes_test
IsAuthenticated
permission_classes
authentication_classes
get_object()
get_queryset()

Potentially interesting:

@csrf_exempt

Example:

rules:
  - id: django-csrf-exempt
    languages:
      - python
    message: Review why CSRF protection is disabled
    severity: WARNING

    pattern: |
      @csrf_exempt
      def $FUNCTION(...):
          ...

CSRF exemption is not automatically exploitable.

docs.title: Flask
docs.text:
Because Flask applications often implement security controls manually, inspect:

before_request
Decorators
Session checks
JWT middleware
Blueprint middleware
Role checks
Ownership checks

Search:

rg -n \
'@.*route|before_request|login_required|authorize|permission|role|session|jwt' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Express
docs.text:
Review:

router.use()
app.use()
authenticate()
authorize()
isAdmin()
requireRole()
requirePermission()

Important:

Middleware order matters.

An authorisation middleware may exist but not cover every route.

docs.title: IDOR / BOLA
docs.text:
The important flow is:

Attacker-Controlled Object ID
          |
          v
Object Lookup
          |
          v
Authorisation?
          |
          v
Sensitive Object

Search:

rg -n \
'findById|findOne|findUnique|findFirst|objects\.get|FindAsync|SingleOrDefault' \
.

OpenGrep becomes particularly valuable after identifying the application's normal authorisation helper.

Example:

checkOwnership()

Then perform variant analysis around code paths that access sensitive objects.

docs.title: Mass Assignment
docs.text:
Example Node.js:

Object.assign(
    user,
    req.body
);

Rule:

rules:
  - id: node-request-body-object-assign
    languages:
      - javascript
      - typescript
    message: Review request-body mass assignment
    severity: WARNING

    pattern: Object.assign($OBJECT, req.body)

Review sensitive fields such as:

role
isAdmin
permissions
tenantId
status
verified
balance
ownerId

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
rules:
  - id: python-jwt-review
    languages:
      - python
    message: Review JWT handling
    severity: INFO

    pattern-either:
      - pattern: jwt.decode(...)
      - pattern: jwt.encode(...)

docs.title: Node.js
docs.text:
rules:
  - id: node-jwt-review
    languages:
      - javascript
      - typescript
    message: Review JWT handling
    severity: INFO

    pattern-either:
      - pattern: jwt.verify(...)
      - pattern: jwt.decode(...)
      - pattern: jwt.sign(...)

Review:

Signature verification
Algorithm restrictions
Issuer
Audience
Expiration
Not-before
Key selection
Key retrieval
Claims
Authorisation

docs.title: OAuth and OIDC
docs.text:
Search:

authorize
callback
redirect_uri
state
nonce
code_verifier
code_challenge
issuer
audience
openid
userinfo

Static analysis can identify handlers and configuration.

Protocol correctness still requires understanding the entire flow.

docs.title: SAML
docs.text:
Search:

SAMLResponse
RelayState
Assertion
Signature
Audience
Recipient
Destination
InResponseTo

Review:

Signature validation
Assertion validation
Audience
Recipient
Destination
Replay
Identity mapping
Authorisation after authentication

docs.title: Password Reset
docs.text:
Use ripgrep first:

rg -ni \
'forgot.?password|reset.?password|password.?reset|reset.?token|recovery' \
.

Then inspect:

Token generation
Token entropy
Token storage
Expiration
Single use
User enumeration
Session invalidation
Password policy
Host-derived links

docs.title: MFA
docs.text:
Search:

totp
otp
mfa
2fa
verifyCode
backupCode
recoveryCode

Review whether MFA is enforced at:

Initial login
Sensitive actions
Session upgrade
Password reset
Account recovery
API authentication

docs.title: Taint Analysis
docs.text:
Pattern rules answer:

Does this code contain something interesting?

Taint analysis asks:

Can untrusted data reach a dangerous operation?

This is one of the most important differences.

SOURCE
   |
   v
Untrusted Data
   |
   v
Transformation
   |
   v
Function
   |
   v
SINK

docs.title: Basic Taint Rule
docs.text:
Conceptually:

rules:
  - id: example-taint
    languages:
      - python

    message: Untrusted data may reach a sensitive sink

    severity: WARNING

    mode: taint

    pattern-sources:
      - pattern: source(...)

    pattern-sinks:
      - pattern: sink(...)

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
A source represents potentially untrusted data.

Examples:

HTTP parameters
Request bodies
Headers
Cookies
Uploaded files
GraphQL arguments
WebSocket messages
gRPC fields
Queue messages
Database-stored attacker data

docs.title: Sinks
docs.text:
A sink represents a security-sensitive operation.

Examples:

SQL execution
OS command execution
Filesystem access
HTTP requests
Template evaluation
Dynamic code execution
HTML rendering
Redirects
Deserialisation
LDAP filters
XML parsing

docs.title: Sanitizers
docs.text:
Taint rules can model sanitizers.

Conceptually:

pattern-sanitizers:
  - pattern: validate(...)

But only model a function as a sanitizer if you understand its guarantees.

A function named:

sanitize()

does not automatically make data safe.

docs.title: Context-Specific Sanitisation
docs.text:
Remember:

HTML encoding
    !=
SQL protection

SQL parameterisation
    !=
Shell escaping

Shell escaping
    !=
URL validation

URL validation
    !=
Path containment

Security controls are context-specific.

docs.title: Flask Command Injection Taint Rule
docs.text:
rules:
  - id: flask-request-to-os-system

    languages:
      - python

    message: Flask request data may reach os.system()

    severity: ERROR

    mode: taint

    pattern-sources:
      - pattern: request.args.get(...)
      - pattern: request.form.get(...)
      - pattern: request.values.get(...)

    pattern-sinks:
      - pattern: os.system(...)

Example:

@app.route("/ping")
def ping():
    host = request.args.get("host")
    os.system("ping -c 1 " + host)
    return "done"

Flow:

request.args.get()
       |
       v
      host
       |
       v
String Construction
       |
       v
os.system()

docs.title: Flask SSRF Taint Rule
docs.text:
rules:
  - id: flask-request-to-http-client

    languages:
      - python

    message: Flask request data may reach an outbound HTTP request

    severity: WARNING

    mode: taint

    pattern-sources:
      - pattern: request.args.get(...)
      - pattern: request.form.get(...)
      - pattern: request.values.get(...)

    pattern-sinks:
      - pattern: requests.get(...)
      - pattern: requests.post(...)
      - pattern: requests.request(...)

This identifies possible flows.

It does not determine whether URL validation prevents SSRF.

docs.title: Cross-Function Taint Analysis
docs.text:
One particularly important OpenGrep capability is:

--taint-intrafile

This enables taint tracking across function boundaries within the same file.

Without it, a taint flow may be limited by function boundaries.

Conceptually:

def get_input():
    return source()

def helper(value):
    return value

def main():
    data = get_input()
    result = helper(data)
    sink(result)

Flow:

source()
   |
   v
get_input()
   |
   v
main()
   |
   v
helper()
   |
   v
sink()

Run:

opengrep scan \
  -f taint-rule.yml \
  example.py \
  --taint-intrafile

This capability is extremely useful for security review because real applications frequently use helper functions.

docs.title: Intrafile Does Not Mean Whole Program
docs.text:
Important distinction:

--taint-intrafile

means cross-function analysis within a file.

Do not automatically interpret it as:

Complete whole-program interprocedural analysis across the repository

Complex cross-file flows may still require:

Manual tracing
Custom rules
CodeQL
Other static analysis
Dynamic validation

docs.title: Cross-Function Example
docs.text:
Suppose:

def get_target():
    return request.args.get("url")

def fetch(url):
    return requests.get(url)

@app.route("/preview")
def preview():
    target = get_target()
    return fetch(target).text

A basic local flow may be difficult for simple taint analysis.

With intrafile cross-function analysis:

request.args
     |
     v
get_target()
     |
     v
preview()
     |
     v
fetch()
     |
     v
requests.get()

becomes analysable within the same file.

docs.title: Higher-Order Functions
docs.text:
OpenGrep's intrafile taint work also includes support for higher-order-function patterns.

This matters especially for JavaScript and TypeScript.

Example:

const input = source();

const values = [input];

values.forEach((value) => {
    sink(value);
});

Conceptually:

source()
   |
   v
Array
   |
   v
forEach()
   |
   v
Callback Parameter
   |
   v
sink()

Modern JavaScript frequently uses:

map()
filter()
reduce()
forEach()
callbacks
custom higher-order functions

Taint analysis that understands these patterns can provide better coverage.

docs.title: Collections
docs.text:
Taint can also move through collections.

Example:

User Input
   |
   v
List / Map
   |
   v
Collection Operation
   |
   v
Retrieved Value
   |
   v
Sink

This matters for:

Java collections
JavaScript arrays
Maps
Lists
Dictionaries

Still validate findings manually.

docs.title: Dataflow Traces
docs.text:
OpenGrep can display data-flow traces for taint findings.

Example:

opengrep scan \
  --dataflow-traces \
  -f rule.yml \
  .

This can make triage significantly easier.

Conceptually:

Source
  |
  v
Assignment
  |
  v
Function
  |
  v
Transformation
  |
  v
Sink

Use the trace as a guide.

Then inspect the actual source code in VS Code.

docs.title: Testing Rules
docs.text:
Security rules should be tested.

Example test:

def vulnerable():
    value = source()

    # ruleid: example-taint
    sink(value)


def safe():
    value = "fixed"

    # ok: example-taint
    sink(value)

Run:

opengrep test \
  --config rule.yml \
  test_rule.py

OpenGrep supports multiple target files for rule testing.

Example:

opengrep test \
  --config rule.yml \
  test_python.py \
  test_python_variants.py

docs.title: Validate Rule Syntax
docs.text:
Validate a rule:

opengrep validate rule.yml

Use this before relying on a new rule.

docs.title: Rule Development Workflow
docs.text:
Write Rule
   |
   v
Validate
   |
   v
Test Positive Cases
   |
   v
Test Negative Cases
   |
   v
Run Against Repository
   |
   v
Review False Positives
   |
   v
Review False Negatives
   |
   v
Refine
   |
   v
Production Rule

docs.title: Positive Tests
docs.text:
Positive tests should cover:

Direct call
Multiline call
Alias
Wrapper
Different argument order
Nested expression
Cross-function flow
Collection flow
Framework-specific variant

docs.title: Negative Tests
docs.text:
Negative tests should cover:

Constant input
Correct parameterisation
Validated input
Correct sanitisation
Safe API
Test-only false positive
Different unrelated API

docs.title: Rule Naming
docs.text:
Use descriptive rule IDs.

Good:

flask-request-to-os-system
django-request-to-raw-sql
spring-request-to-processbuilder
dotnet-request-to-httpclient
node-request-to-child-process
javascript-location-to-innerhtml

Avoid:

rule1
test
bad
vulnerability

docs.title: Variant Analysis
docs.text:
One of the strongest uses of OpenGrep is variant analysis.

Confirmed Vulnerability
        |
        v
Understand Root Cause
        |
        v
Identify Code Pattern
        |
        v
Create OpenGrep Rule
        |
        v
Scan Repository
        |
        v
Find Similar Instances

This often provides more value than generic security rules.

docs.title: Example Variant Analysis
docs.text:
Suppose manual review finds:

public void executeReport(
    String command
) throws Exception {

    Runtime.getRuntime().exec(command);
}

The application repeatedly uses:

executeReport(...)

Create:

rules:
  - id: application-execute-report
    languages:
      - java
    message: Review custom command execution helper
    severity: ERROR

    pattern: executeReport(...)

Scan:

opengrep scan \
  -f rules/application-execute-report.yml \
  .

Now inspect every caller.

docs.title: Variant Analysis Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm one vulnerability manually

2. Determine the vulnerable primitive

3. Identify helper functions

4. Identify wrappers

5. Write structural rule

6. Write taint rule if useful

7. Create positive tests

8. Create negative tests

9. Run OpenGrep

10. Triage results

11. Refine rule

12. Scan related authorised repositories

13. Use CodeQL if the flow is too complex

docs.title: Project-Specific Rules
docs.text:
Generic rule:

Find os.system()

Project-specific rule:

Find every call to executeDiagnosticCommand()

Generic:

Find requests.get()

Project-specific:

Find every call to fetchExternalResource()

Generic:

Find cursor.execute()

Project-specific:

Find every call to runReportQuery()

Once the architecture is understood, project-specific rules usually become much more valuable.

docs.title: Authentication Variant Analysis
docs.text:
Suppose the normal pattern is:

@PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('ADMIN')")
public void deleteUser(...) {

During review, you may want to identify related sensitive operations and compare their authorisation.

Do not automatically write a rule that assumes every function without the annotation is vulnerable.

Authorisation may exist:

At controller level
At class level
In middleware
In filters
In service logic
At API gateway level

Missing-control analysis requires careful architecture knowledge.

docs.title: Tenant Isolation
docs.text:
For multi-tenant applications, look for:

tenantId
organisationId
organizationId
accountId
customerId
workspaceId

Model:

Authenticated User
      |
      v
Tenant Context
      |
      v
Object ID
      |
      v
Database Query
      |
      v
Tenant Constraint?

A useful review question is:

Does every sensitive object query enforce the tenant boundary?

OpenGrep can help search for repository methods that omit the expected tenant parameter.

docs.title: Business Logic
docs.text:
Static analysis is weaker at generic business logic.

Examples:

Coupon reuse
Price manipulation
Approval bypass
Account-state bypass
Workflow skipping
Duplicate redemption
Negative quantity
Tenant workflow errors

But once a broken pattern is known:

Manual Discovery
      |
      v
Broken Function
      |
      v
Structural Pattern
      |
      v
OpenGrep Rule
      |
      v
Variant Search

becomes powerful.

docs.title: Race Conditions
docs.text:
OpenGrep can help locate:

Read-modify-write patterns
Transaction handling
Locking
Atomic operations
Concurrency checks

But race-condition exploitability usually depends on runtime behaviour.

Review:

Transactions
Isolation levels
Database constraints
Optimistic locking
Distributed locks
External services

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
OpenGrep can identify:

Rate-limit middleware
Throttle decorators
Quota functions
Login attempt counters
Password reset limits
OTP attempt limits

But:

No rate limiter in source
      !=
No rate limiting in production

Controls may exist in:

CDN
WAF
API gateway
Reverse proxy
Service mesh

docs.title: HTTP Security Headers
docs.text:
Search:

Content-Security-Policy
Strict-Transport-Security
X-Frame-Options
X-Content-Type-Options
Referrer-Policy
Permissions-Policy

Remember:

Missing in application source
        !=
Missing in HTTP response

Infrastructure may inject headers.

docs.title: Host Header and Proxy Trust
docs.text:
Review:

Host
X-Forwarded-Host
X-Forwarded-Proto
Forwarded
trust proxy
absolute URL generation
password reset URLs
OAuth callback URLs

Potential flow:

Host Header
    |
    v
Framework
    |
    v
Absolute URL
    |
    v
Password Reset Email

docs.title: HTTP Request Smuggling
docs.text:
OpenGrep cannot prove HTTP request smuggling merely by inspecting application code.

It can help locate:

Custom HTTP parsers
Content-Length processing
Transfer-Encoding processing
Proxy code
Header rewriting

Actual exploitability depends on the entire HTTP processing chain.

docs.title: Web Cache Security
docs.text:
Search:

Cache-Control
Vary
cache keys
custom caching
reverse proxy configuration
CDN configuration

Cache poisoning and deception often require runtime testing.

docs.title: GraphQL
docs.text:
Search:

Resolver
Mutation
Query
Subscription
GraphQL
DataFetcher

Model:

GraphQL Argument
      |
      v
Resolver
      |
      v
Authorisation
      |
      v
Service
      |
      v
Database

Object-level authorisation is particularly important.

docs.title: gRPC
docs.text:
Review:

.proto files
service definitions
RPC methods
interceptors
authentication
authorisation
message fields

Model:

gRPC Message
     |
     v
RPC Handler
     |
     v
Authorisation
     |
     v
Service
     |
     v
Sensitive Sink

docs.title: WebSockets
docs.text:
Review:

Connection authentication
Message handlers
Message-level authorisation
Room access
Channel access
Subscriptions
Object IDs
Input validation

Authentication during the initial handshake does not automatically authorise every subsequent operation.

docs.title: Background Jobs
docs.text:
Static analysis should not stop at HTTP controllers.

Search:

cron
scheduler
worker
queue
consumer
listener
job
task
background

Potential second-order flow:

HTTP Request
     |
     v
Database
     |
     v
Queue
     |
     v
Worker
     |
     v
Dangerous Sink

docs.title: Second-Order Vulnerabilities
docs.text:
Example:

Attacker Input
      |
      v
Stored in Database
      |
      v
Later Retrieved
      |
      v
Background Worker
      |
      v
Process Execution

Simple direct taint analysis may not model every persistence boundary.

Always ask:

Who originally controlled this data?

docs.title: Trust Boundaries
docs.text:
Do not automatically trust data because it comes from:

Database
Cache
Message queue
Internal API
File
Environment
Microservice
Webhook

The important question is:

What was the original source?

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
OpenGrep can search for suspicious hardcoded credentials.

But dedicated tools should also be used.

Examples:

TruffleHog
Git history analysis
Repository search
Secret scanners

Do not report every:

password =
token =
secret =

as a vulnerability.

Determine whether the value is an actual credential and what it can access.

docs.title: Cryptography
docs.text:
Search:

MD5
SHA1
DES
ECB
static IV
hardcoded key
random
PRNG
TLS verification disabled
certificate validation bypass

Context matters.

For example:

SHA-1 used for a non-security cache key

is different from:

SHA-1 used for password storage

docs.title: Dependency Security
docs.text:
OpenGrep is primarily source-code static analysis.

Use dedicated dependency tools as well:

OSV-Scanner
npm audit
pip-audit
Trivy
Composer audit
Maven tooling
Gradle tooling
NuGet tooling

Use OpenGrep to identify:

Unsafe library usage
Deprecated security APIs
Application-specific misuse

docs.title: Ignore Files
docs.text:
OpenGrep supports .semgrepignore compatibility.

Example:

node_modules/
vendor/
dist/
build/
coverage/
generated/

Be careful when excluding:

vendor/
generated/
third_party/

because security-sensitive code can exist there.

Review exclusions before scanning.

docs.title: Custom Ignore Filename
docs.text:
OpenGrep supports specifying a custom ignore file.

Conceptually:

opengrep scan \
  --semgrepignore-filename=<file> \
  ...

This can be useful when maintaining separate:

Development exclusions
Security-review exclusions

docs.title: Include and Exclude Paths
docs.text:
Example:

opengrep scan \
  --config rules/ \
  --include='src/**' \
  --exclude='**/test/**' \
  .

Review what you exclude.

Tests can sometimes reveal:

Hidden endpoints
Default credentials
Security assumptions
Internal APIs
Feature flags
Debug functionality

docs.title: force-exclude
docs.text:
OpenGrep also provides:

--force-exclude

for applying include/exclude behaviour to explicitly passed targets where appropriate.

Example concept:

opengrep scan \
  --force-exclude \
  --exclude='**/vendor/**' \
  -f rule.yml \
  .

Check current CLI help for exact behaviour in your installed version.

docs.title: JSON Output
docs.text:
For automation:

opengrep scan \
  -f rules/ \
  --json \
  -o opengrep.json \
  .

JSON is useful for:

Scripts
Dashboards
Triage tooling
Result comparison
CI/CD

docs.title: SARIF Output
docs.text:
SARIF integrates well with security tooling and code-scanning systems.

opengrep scan \
  -f rules/ \
  --sarif \
  -o opengrep.sarif \
  .

docs.title: Data-Flow Output
docs.text:
For taint analysis:

opengrep scan \
  --dataflow-traces \
  -f taint-rule.yml \
  .

This helps show:

Source
  |
  v
Propagation
  |
  v
Sink

docs.title: Save Assessment Evidence
docs.text:
Recommended:

review/
├── opengrep/
│   ├── initial.json
│   ├── sinks.json
│   ├── taint.json
│   ├── intrafile.json
│   ├── variants.json
│   ├── results.sarif
│   └── triage.md
│
├── ripgrep/
│   ├── routes.txt
│   ├── sources.txt
│   └── sinks.txt
│
└── findings/

docs.title: Record Tool Version
docs.text:
Always record:

opengrep --version

Example evidence:

Tool:
OpenGrep

Version:
<version>

Repository:
<repository>

Branch:
<branch>

Commit:
<commit hash>

Rules:
rules/

Date:
<assessment date>

This improves reproducibility.

docs.title: Triage Template
docs.text:
ID:
OG-001

Rule:
flask-request-to-os-system

File:
src/routes/tools.py

Line:
84

Potential Vulnerability:
Command Injection

Source:
request.args.get("host")

Sink:
os.system()

Reachable:
Yes / No / Unknown

Attacker Controlled:
Yes / No / Unknown

Validation:
None / Present / Unknown

Sanitisation:
None / Present / Unknown

Security Controls:
...

Data Flow:
...

Dynamic Validation:
...

Status:
Investigating / Confirmed / False Positive

Notes:
...

docs.title: Finding Validation Model
docs.text:
OpenGrep Match
      |
      v
Reachable?
      |
      +--> No
      |     |
      |     v
      |   Reject
      |
      v
Attacker-Controlled Source?
      |
      +--> No
      |     |
      |     v
      |   Review Trust Boundary
      |
      v

docs.title: OpenGrep and Semgrep
docs.text:
OpenGrep was forked from Semgrep and aims to maintain compatibility with Semgrep rules.

This makes it possible to reuse many existing rule files.

Conceptually:

rules/
   |
   +--> Semgrep
   |
   +--> OpenGrep

But test important rules in both engines if both are part of your workflow.

Reasons include:

Parser differences
Engine evolution
Taint behaviour
CLI differences
Feature divergence
Bug fixes
Language support differences

Do not assume permanent one-to-one equivalence.

docs.title: ripgrep for Security Source Code Review
docs.text:
ripgrep (rg) is one of the most useful tools for manual security source code review.

It provides extremely fast recursive searching across source repositories and supports:

Literal searches
Regular expressions
File-type filtering
Directory exclusions
Context lines
Case-insensitive searches
Multiple patterns
Machine-readable output

For security review, ripgrep is particularly useful for locating:

Routes and endpoints
User-controlled input
Authentication
Authorisation
Database queries
Operating system commands
File operations
Outbound HTTP requests
Template rendering
Deserialisation
XML parsing
Redirects
Secrets
Cryptographic operations
Security configuration
GraphQL
gRPC
WebSockets
Background jobs
Message queues

The fundamental workflow is:

Repository
    |
    v
Identify Technology
    |
    v
Search Entry Points
    |
    v
Search Sources
    |
    v
Search Security Controls
    |
    v
Search Dangerous Sinks
    |
    v
Open Candidate in VS Code
    |
    v
Trace Source -> Sink
    |
    v
Determine Exploitability

Authorised Security Testing

Use these techniques only against source code, applications and environments for which you have explicit authorisation. A search result is a review candidate, not proof of a vulnerability.

docs.title: Core Principle
docs.text:
The most important rule when using ripgrep is:

rg match
   !=
vulnerability

For example:

rg -n 'ProcessBuilder' .

may identify:

new ProcessBuilder(
    "/usr/bin/convert",
    inputFile,
    outputFile
);

The presence of ProcessBuilder does not automatically prove command injection.

You must determine:

Can an attacker control the executable?

Can an attacker control arguments?

Is a shell involved?

Can argument injection occur?

Is the path attacker-controlled?

What program is being invoked?

What does the invoked program do with its arguments?

Similarly:

HttpClient
    !=
SSRF

createNativeQuery
    !=
SQL Injection

innerHTML
    !=
XSS

ObjectInputStream
    !=
Exploitable Deserialisation

ripgrep finds interesting code.

The reviewer determines whether it is vulnerable.

docs.title: Debian / Ubuntu / Kali Linux
docs.text:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install ripgrep

Verify:

rg --version

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
Search recursively:

rg 'password' .

Show line numbers:

rg -n 'password' .

Case-insensitive:

rg -ni 'password' .

Show filenames only:

rg -l 'password' .

Count matches per file:

rg -c 'password' .

Fixed-string search:

rg -F 'Runtime.getRuntime().exec' .

docs.title: Search Multiple Patterns
docs.text:
Use regex alternation:

rg -n \
'password|secret|token|api_key' \
.

Or multiple -e expressions:

rg -n \
-e 'password' \
-e 'secret' \
-e 'token' \
.

docs.title: Context Lines
docs.text:
Show three lines before and after:

rg -n -C 3 'ProcessBuilder' .

Before:

rg -n -B 5 'ProcessBuilder' .

After:

rg -n -A 5 'ProcessBuilder' .

This is useful when reviewing:

Sources
Validation
Function arguments
Security controls

docs.title: File Filtering
docs.text:
Search Java only:

rg -n 'ProcessBuilder' \
-g '*.java' \
.

C#:

rg -n 'Process.Start' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

PHP:

rg -n 'shell_exec' \
-g '*.php' \
.

Python:

rg -n 'subprocess' \
-g '*.py' \
.

JavaScript and TypeScript:

rg -n 'child_process' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
-g '*.jsx' \
-g '*.tsx' \
.

docs.title: Excluding Noise
docs.text:
Large repositories often contain:

node_modules
vendor
target
build
dist
bin
obj
coverage
generated files

Exclude them:

rg -n \
'password' \
. \
-g '!node_modules/**' \
-g '!vendor/**' \
-g '!target/**' \
-g '!build/**' \
-g '!dist/**' \
-g '!bin/**' \
-g '!obj/**'

docs.title: Recommended .rgignore
docs.text:
For repeated source review, create:

.rgignore

Example:

node_modules/
vendor/
target/
build/
dist/
bin/
obj/
coverage/
.next/
.nuxt/

Be careful with exclusions.

Do not hide security-relevant:

Configuration
Templates
Deployment files
Generated API code
Custom vendored code

without first understanding the repository.

docs.title: Hidden Files
docs.text:
By default, hidden files are generally skipped.

Include them with:

rg --hidden 'secret' .

This can be important for:

.env
.github/
.gitlab/
Docker configuration
CI/CD configuration

Avoid blindly searching .git internals unless Git history analysis is intentionally required.

Example:

rg --hidden \
-g '!.git/**' \
'secret' \
.

docs.title: List Files
docs.text:
List files rg considers searchable:

rg --files

Java files:

rg --files -g '*.java'

Configuration:

rg --files | grep -Ei \
'application|config|settings|security|docker|compose|nginx'

docs.text:
Do not begin with one enormous regex.

Perform separate passes:

1. Repository reconnaissance
2. Route discovery
3. Source discovery
4. Authentication
5. Authorisation
6. Input validation
7. Database sinks
8. Command execution
9. SSRF
10. Files
11. Uploads
12. XML
13. Deserialisation
14. Templates
15. XSS

17. Host/proxy handling
18. Secrets
19. Cryptography

22. APIs
23. Dependencies
24. Variant analysis

docs.title: Repository Reconnaissance
docs.text:
Start with:

rg --files

Find common project manifests:

rg --files | grep -E \
'(^|/)(pom\.xml|build\.gradle|build\.gradle\.kts|package\.json|composer\.json|requirements\.txt|pyproject\.toml|.*\.csproj|.*\.sln)$'

Find configuration:

rg --files | grep -Ei \
'application\.(yml|yaml|properties)|appsettings.*\.json|settings\.py|\.env|docker|compose|nginx|apache|security|config'

docs.title: Identify Frameworks
docs.text:
Search dependency manifests:

rg -ni \
'spring-boot|spring-security|django|flask|express|aspnetcore|laravel|symfony|fastapi' \
.

This provides clues about which source and sink searches should be prioritised.

docs.title: Search TODO and Security Comments
docs.text:
rg -ni \
'TODO|FIXME|HACK|XXX|temporary|workaround|bypass|remove before production' \
.

These are not vulnerabilities.

They can identify high-value review areas.

Search security-related comments:

rg -ni \
'security|sanitize|sanitise|validate|trusted|permission|admin|authori[sz]e|authentication' \
.

Never trust a comment without inspecting the implementation.

docs.title: Route Discovery
docs.text: Routes define much of the externally reachable attack surface.

docs.title: Java / Spring Routes
docs.text:
rg -n \
'@(RequestMapping|GetMapping|PostMapping|PutMapping|PatchMapping|DeleteMapping|RestController|Controller)\b' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Search functional WebFlux routes:

rg -n \
'RouterFunction|RouterFunctions\.route|\bGET\(|\bPOST\(|\bPUT\(|\bPATCH\(|\bDELETE\(' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Servlet/JAX-RS style:

rg -n \
'@WebServlet|@Path|@GET\b|@POST\b|@PUT\b|@PATCH\b|@DELETE\b' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Remember that Spring paths can be composed from:

Class-level @RequestMapping
        +
Method-level @GetMapping

So a match may not contain the complete URL.

docs.title: .NET / ASP.NET Core Routes
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\[(Route|HttpGet|HttpPost|HttpPut|HttpPatch|HttpDelete|HttpHead|HttpOptions)' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

Minimal APIs:

rg -n \
'\.(MapGet|MapPost|MapPut|MapPatch|MapDelete|MapMethods|MapGroup)\(' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

Controllers:

rg -n \
'ControllerBase|Controller\b|\[ApiController\]' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: PHP Routes
docs.text:
Framework-specific route definitions commonly include patterns such as:

rg -n \
'Route::(get|post|put|patch|delete|any|match)|->addRoute|->map\(' \
-g '*.php' \
.

Also inspect:

routes/
controllers/
public/index.php

docs.title: Django Routes
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\bpath\(|\bre_path\(|\binclude\(' \
-g '*.py' \
.

Search views:

rg -n \
'def .*request|class .*View|APIView|ViewSet|ModelViewSet' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Flask Routes
docs.text:
rg -n \
'@(app|[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\.route\(' \
-g '*.py' \
.

Also:

rg -n \
'add_url_rule\(' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js / Express Routes
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\b(app|router)\.(get|post|put|patch|delete|options|head|all)\(' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

Search router mounting:

rg -n \
'\bapp\.use\(|\brouter\.use\(' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

A complete route may be composed from:

app.use("/api", router)
        +
router.get("/users/:id")

Result:

/api/users/:id

docs.title: Route Inventory
docs.text:
Record results as:

Method Route Handler Auth Authz Input GET /users/{id} getUser Yes Review Path POST /upload upload Yes User File POST /login login No N/A Body GET /fetch fetch Yes Review URL

This transforms search results into an attack-surface model.

docs.title: Source Discovery
docs.text: A source is where potentially attacker-controlled data enters the application.

docs.title: Java / Spring Sources
docs.text:
rg -n \
'@RequestParam|@PathVariable|@RequestBody|@RequestHeader|@CookieValue|MultipartFile' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Servlet sources:

rg -n \
'getParameter\(|getParameterValues\(|getParameterMap\(|getHeader\(|getHeaders\(|getCookies\(|getInputStream\(|getReader\(|getRequestURI\(|getQueryString\(|getServerName\(' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET Sources
docs.text:
rg -n \
'Request\.(Query|Form|Headers|Cookies|Body)|\[From(Query|Route|Body|Header|Form)\]|RouteData|HttpContext\.Request' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

File uploads:

rg -n \
'IFormFile|IFormFileCollection|Request\.Form\.Files' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: PHP Sources
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\$_GET|\$_POST|\$_REQUEST|\$_COOKIE|\$_FILES|\$_SERVER' \
-g '*.php' \
.

Input stream:

rg -n \
'php://input|filter_input\(' \
-g '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Django Sources
docs.text:
rg -n \
'request\.(GET|POST|FILES|COOKIES|headers|body|META)' \
-g '*.py' \
.

Django REST Framework:

rg -n \
'request\.(data|query_params|FILES|auth|user)' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Flask Sources
docs.text:
rg -n \
'request\.(args|form|json|files|headers|cookies|data|values)|request\.get_json\(' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js / Express Sources
docs.text:
rg -n \
'req\.(query|params|body|headers|cookies|signedCookies|file|files)' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

docs.title: Browser JavaScript Sources
docs.text:
rg -n \
'location\.(href|search|hash)|document\.(URL|documentURI|referrer)|window\.name|localStorage|sessionStorage|postMessage|message\.data|event\.data' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
-g '*.jsx' \
-g '*.tsx' \
.

docs.title: Authentication Discovery
docs.text:
Search generally:

rg -ni \
'login|logout|authenticate|authentication|credential|password|session|jwt|bearer|oauth|oidc|saml|mfa|totp|otp' \
.

docs.title: Java / Spring Authentication
docs.text:
rg -n \
'SecurityFilterChain|HttpSecurity|AuthenticationManager|AuthenticationProvider|UserDetailsService|PasswordEncoder|UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter|OncePerRequestFilter|oauth2Login|oauth2ResourceServer|saml2Login' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET Authentication
docs.text:
rg -n \
'AddAuthentication|UseAuthentication|AddJwtBearer|AddCookie|SignInAsync|SignOutAsync|ClaimsPrincipal|PasswordHasher|AddOpenIdConnect|AddOAuth' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: Django Authentication
docs.text:
rg -n \
'authenticate\(|login\(|logout\(|login_required|AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS|AuthenticationMiddleware' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Flask Authentication
docs.text:
rg -n \
'login_user|logout_user|login_required|LoginManager|current_user|check_password_hash|generate_password_hash' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js Authentication
docs.text:
rg -n \
'passport|jsonwebtoken|jwt\.verify|jwt\.sign|bcrypt|argon2|express-session|cookie-session|req\.user|isAuthenticated' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

docs.title: Authorisation Discovery
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'authori[sz]e|permission|role|policy|access.?control|isAdmin|is_admin|ownership|tenant|hasRole|hasAuthority' \
.

docs.title: Java / Spring Authorisation
docs.text:
rg -n \
'authorizeHttpRequests|requestMatchers|permitAll|authenticated|hasRole|hasAuthority|@PreAuthorize|@PostAuthorize|@Secured|@RolesAllowed|@EnableMethodSecurity' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Pay special attention to:

permitAll()

Search:

rg -n \
'permitAll\(' \
-g '*.java' \
.

A permitAll() match is not automatically a vulnerability.

Determine which routes it affects.

docs.title: .NET Authorisation
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\[Authorize|\[AllowAnonymous|AddAuthorization|RequireAuthorization|RequireRole|RequireClaim|AuthorizationPolicy|IAuthorizationHandler' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: Django Authorisation
docs.text:
rg -n \
'permission_required|user_passes_test|has_perm|has_perms|PermissionRequiredMixin|UserPassesTestMixin|IsAdminUser|IsAuthenticated|permission_classes' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Flask Authorisation
docs.text:
Flask applications often implement custom authorisation.

Search:

rg -ni \
'permission|role|admin|authori[sz]|current_user|owner|tenant' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js Authorisation
docs.text:
rg -ni \
'permission|role|isAdmin|authorize|authorise|owner|tenant|req\.user' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

docs.title: IDOR / BOLA Candidates
docs.text: Search object lookups.

docs.title: Java
docs.text:
rg -n \
'findById\(|getReferenceById\(|getById\(|findOne\(' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET
docs.text:
rg -n \
'FindAsync\(|Find\(|FirstOrDefaultAsync|SingleOrDefaultAsync|FirstAsync|SingleAsync' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: Django
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\.objects\.(get|filter)|get_object_or_404|get_queryset' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js
docs.text:
rg -n \
'findById|findOne|findUnique|findFirst|findByPk' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

Then ask:

Where is ownership checked?

Where is tenant isolation enforced?

Where is permission checked?

The lookup itself is not the vulnerability.

docs.title: Input Validation
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'validate|validator|sanitize|sanitise|schema|allowlist|whitelist|regex|pattern|constraint' \
.

docs.title: Java Validation
docs.text:
rg -n \
'@Valid|@Validated|@NotNull|@NotBlank|@NotEmpty|@Size|@Pattern|@Email|ConstraintValidator' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET Validation
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\[Required|\[StringLength|\[MaxLength|\[MinLength|\[RegularExpression|ModelState\.IsValid|FluentValidation|AbstractValidator' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: Django Validation
docs.text:
rg -n \
'clean\(|clean_[A-Za-z0-9_]+\(|validators|is_valid\(|Serializer|Form\b|ModelForm' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Flask Validation
docs.text:
rg -ni \
'validate|validator|marshmallow|pydantic|wtforms|schema' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js Validation
docs.text:
rg -n \
'joi|zod|express-validator|ajv|yup|validator\.|validate\(' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

Validation is not automatically equivalent to:

SQL parameterisation
Output encoding
Authorisation
Command safety

docs.title: Java JDBC
docs.text:
rg -n \
'Statement|PreparedStatement|executeQuery\(|executeUpdate\(|execute\(' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Focus particularly on:

Statement
String concatenation
Dynamic SQL fragments

docs.title: Java JPA / Hibernate
docs.text:
rg -n \
'createQuery\(|createNativeQuery\(|Session\.createQuery|@Query|nativeQuery\s*=\s*true' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Spring JDBC:

rg -n \
'JdbcTemplate|NamedParameterJdbcTemplate|queryForObject\(|queryForList\(|update\(' \
-g '*.java' \
.

These APIs can be used safely or unsafely.

Inspect how the query is built and how parameters are bound.

docs.title: .NET SQL
docs.text:
rg -n \
'SqlCommand|DbCommand|FromSqlRaw|ExecuteSqlRaw|SqlQueryRaw|FromSqlInterpolated|ExecuteSqlInterpolated|QueryAsync|ExecuteAsync' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

Look for string construction:

rg -n \
'\$".*(SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE)|string\.Format\(.*(SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE)|\+.*(SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE)' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

Review manually because multiline construction can evade simple regexes.

docs.title: PHP SQL
docs.text:
rg -n \
'mysqli_query\(|mysqli_real_query\(|->query\(|->exec\(|->prepare\(' \
-g '*.php' \
.

Search SQL strings:

rg -ni \
'SELECT .*FROM|INSERT INTO|UPDATE .* SET|DELETE FROM' \
-g '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Django SQL
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\.raw\(|RawSQL\(|\.extra\(|cursor\.execute\(|cursor\.executemany\(' \
-g '*.py' \
.

Normal ORM queries are not automatically immune to every injection-style problem, but raw SQL and dynamic query construction deserve additional attention.

docs.title: Flask / Python SQL
docs.text:
rg -n \
'cursor\.execute\(|cursor\.executemany\(|text\(|execute\(|executemany\(' \
-g '*.py' \
.

Look for interpolation:

rg -n \
'f["'\''].*(SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE)|\.format\(.*|%s.*%' \
-g '*.py' \
.

Expect false positives.

docs.title: Node.js SQL
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\.query\(|\.execute\(|\$queryRaw|\$executeRaw|sequelize\.query|knex\.raw' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

Prisma raw APIs deserve review, particularly unsafe raw query construction.

docs.title: Java / MongoDB
docs.text:
rg -n \
'MongoTemplate|BasicQuery|Document\.parse|Criteria\.where|MongoCollection|Filters\.' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Look for attacker-controlled:

Raw JSON
Mongo operators
Query documents
Field names
Operators

docs.title: Python / MongoDB
docs.text:
rg -n \
'find_one\(|find\(|update_one\(|update_many\(|delete_one\(|delete_many\(|aggregate\(' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js / MongoDB
docs.text:
rg -n \
'findOne\(|find\(|findById\(|updateOne\(|updateMany\(|deleteOne\(|aggregate\(' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

Look for:

req.body passed directly into query objects
Raw operators
$where
$regex
$ne
$gt
$where

Search:

rg -n \
'\$(where|ne|gt|gte|lt|lte|regex|in|nin|or|and)' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
-g '*.json' \
.

docs.title: Java
docs.text:
rg -n \
'LdapTemplate|DirContext|InitialDirContext|SearchControls|\.search\(' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Search LDAP filters:

rg -n \
'\(&|\(\||\(uid=|\(cn=|\(mail=|\(objectClass=' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET
docs.text:
rg -n \
'DirectorySearcher|DirectoryEntry|System\.DirectoryServices|SearchRoot|Filter\s*=' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: PHP
docs.text:
rg -n \
'ldap_search\(|ldap_list\(|ldap_read\(|ldap_bind\(' \
-g '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
rg -n \
'ldap\.search|search_s\(|search_ext|ldap3|search_filter' \
-g '*.py' \
.

Always inspect filter construction and escaping.

docs.title: Java
docs.text:
rg -n \
'Runtime\.getRuntime\(\)\.exec|ProcessBuilder|ProcessHandle' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Shell invocation:

rg -n \
'/bin/sh|/bin/bash|bash|sh -c|cmd\.exe|cmd /c|powershell|pwsh' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET
docs.text:
rg -n \
'Process\.Start|ProcessStartInfo|System\.Diagnostics\.Process' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

Shell invocation:

rg -ni \
'cmd\.exe|/c|powershell|pwsh|/bin/sh|bash' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: PHP
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\b(system|exec|shell_exec|passthru|popen|proc_open|pcntl_exec)\s*\(' \
-g '*.php' \
.

Backticks can also execute commands in PHP and may require manual review.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
rg -n \
'os\.system\(|os\.popen\(|subprocess\.(run|Popen|call|check_call|check_output|getoutput|getstatusoutput)\(' \
-g '*.py' \
.

High-interest shell use:

rg -n \
'shell\s*=\s*True' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js
docs.text:
rg -n \
'child_process|exec\(|execSync\(|execFile\(|execFileSync\(|spawn\(|spawnSync\(' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

docs.title: Dynamic Code Execution
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'\beval\(|\bexec\(|new Function|Function\(|ScriptEngine|GroovyShell|CSharpScript|CodeDomProvider|compile\(' \
.

Interpret matches according to language.

For example:

Python exec()

and:

PHP exec()

are completely different security sinks.

Language-specific searches are preferable.

docs.title: Java Dynamic Execution
docs.text:
rg -n \
'ScriptEngine|ScriptEngineManager|GroovyShell|Class\.forName|Method\.invoke|SpelExpressionParser|parseExpression' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Reflection is not automatically unsafe.

Determine whether attacker-controlled data selects:

Classes
Methods
Expressions
Scripts

docs.title: Python Dynamic Execution
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\beval\(|\bexec\(|compile\(' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: JavaScript Dynamic Execution
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\beval\(|new Function|Function\(|setTimeout\(|setInterval\(|vm\.runIn|vm\.runInNewContext|vm\.runInThisContext' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

String-based timers deserve more attention than function callbacks.

docs.title: Java / Spring
docs.text:
rg -n \
'SpelExpressionParser|parseExpression|Expression\.getValue|FreeMarker|Velocity|Thymeleaf|Pebble|TemplateEngine|process\(' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Search dynamic view names:

rg -n \
'return\s+["'\'']redirect:|return\s+.*view|ModelAndView|setViewName' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Manual context is essential.

docs.title: Flask / Jinja
docs.text:
rg -n \
'render_template_string\(|Environment\(|Template\(|from_string\(' \
-g '*.py' \
.

Normal:

render_template("page.html", value=user_input)

does not mean SSTI merely because user input reaches template data.

Focus on attacker influence over:

Template source
Template expression
Dynamic template construction

docs.title: PHP Templates
docs.text:
Search framework/template-specific functions:

rg -ni \
'twig|blade|smarty|template|render' \
-g '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Java
docs.text:
rg -n \
'java\.net\.URL|new URL\(|URI\.create|URLConnection|openConnection\(|HttpClient|HttpRequest|RestTemplate|RestClient|WebClient|OkHttpClient|CloseableHttpClient' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET
docs.text:
rg -n \
'HttpClient|WebClient|WebRequest|HttpWebRequest|RestClient|SendAsync|GetAsync|GetStringAsync' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: PHP
docs.text:
rg -n \
'curl_init\(|curl_setopt\(|curl_exec\(|file_get_contents\(|fopen\(' \
-g '*.php' \
.

Remember that file APIs may support URLs depending on configuration and usage.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
rg -n \
'requests\.(get|post|put|patch|delete|request)|httpx\.(get|post|put|patch|delete|request)|urlopen\(|urllib\.request|aiohttp|ClientSession' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js
docs.text:
rg -n \
'axios\.|fetch\(|http\.request|https\.request|http\.get|https\.get|got\(|request\(' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

For every candidate examine:

URL source
Scheme validation
Host validation
Port validation
DNS resolution
Redirects
Internal networks
Cloud metadata
Egress controls

docs.title: Java
docs.text:
rg -n \
'new File\(|Paths\.get\(|Path\.of\(|\.resolve\(|Files\.(read|write|copy|move|delete)|FileInputStream|FileOutputStream' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET
docs.text:
rg -n \
'Path\.(Combine|Join|GetFullPath)|File\.(Open|Read|Write|Delete|Move|Copy)|Directory\.' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: PHP
docs.text:
rg -n \
'file_get_contents\(|file_put_contents\(|fopen\(|readfile\(|unlink\(|rename\(|copy\(' \
-g '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\bopen\(|Path\(|pathlib|os\.path\.(join|abspath|realpath)|send_file\(|send_from_directory\(' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js
docs.text:
rg -n \
'fs\.(readFile|readFileSync|writeFile|writeFileSync|createReadStream|createWriteStream|unlink|rename)|path\.(join|resolve|normalize)' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

Do not assume:

Path.resolve()
Path.Combine()
Path.join()

provides containment.

Review the final normalized/canonical path and base-directory boundary.

docs.title: File Inclusion Candidates
docs.text:
PHP is particularly relevant:

rg -n \
'\b(include|include_once|require|require_once)\s*\(' \
-g '*.php' \
.

Trace whether attacker-controlled data influences the included path.

docs.title: Java
docs.text:
rg -n \
'MultipartFile|getOriginalFilename\(|transferTo\(|getInputStream\(' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET
docs.text:
rg -n \
'IFormFile|CopyToAsync|CopyTo\(|FileName|OpenReadStream' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: PHP
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\$_FILES|move_uploaded_file\(|is_uploaded_file\(' \
-g '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Django / Flask
docs.text:
rg -n \
'request\.FILES|request\.files|save\(|secure_filename|FileField|ImageField' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js
docs.text:
rg -n \
'multer|formidable|busboy|express-fileupload|req\.file|req\.files' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

Review:

Original filename
Generated filename
Extension
MIME type
Content
Size
Storage location
Web accessibility
Permissions
Downstream processing
Archive extraction

docs.title: Archive Extraction and Zip Slip
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'ZipInputStream|ZipEntry|ZipFile|extractall|extract\(|unzip|adm-zip|yauzl|archiver|ZipArchive' \
.

Trace archive entry names into filesystem paths.

docs.title: Java
docs.text:
rg -n \
'DocumentBuilderFactory|SAXParserFactory|XMLInputFactory|TransformerFactory|SchemaFactory|XMLReader|SAXParser|Unmarshaller|JAXBContext' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET
docs.text:
rg -n \
'XmlDocument|XmlReader|XmlTextReader|XDocument|XmlResolver|DtdProcessing' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: PHP
docs.text:
rg -n \
'DOMDocument|SimpleXML|simplexml_load|XMLReader|xml_parse' \
-g '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
rg -n \
'xml\.etree|ElementTree|lxml|etree|xml\.dom|xml\.sax|BeautifulSoup' \
-g '*.py' \
.

Parser presence does not prove XXE.

Review:

Parser
Version
DTD handling
External entity handling
Network access
Configuration
Input trust

docs.title: Java
docs.text:
rg -n \
'ObjectInputStream|readObject\(|readUnshared\(|XMLDecoder|XStream|activateDefaultTyping|enableDefaultTyping|ObjectMapper|Yaml\(' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Do not treat:

ObjectMapper.readValue()

as inherently unsafe.

Investigate:

Polymorphic typing
Allowed classes
Trust boundary
Library version
Custom type resolution

docs.title: .NET
docs.text:
rg -n \
'BinaryFormatter|LosFormatter|ObjectStateFormatter|NetDataContractSerializer|JavaScriptSerializer|TypeNameHandling|Deserialize\(' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: PHP
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\bunserialize\(' \
-g '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
rg -n \
'pickle\.(load|loads)|cPickle|yaml\.load\(|marshal\.loads|shelve\.' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Java / JSP
docs.text:
rg -n \
'<%=|<c:out|response\.getWriter\(\)|PrintWriter|\.write\(|\.print\(' \
-g '*.jsp' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Thymeleaf:

rg -n \
'th:text|th:utext' \
-g '*.html' \
.

th:text and th:utext have different output behavior and should not be treated as equivalent.

docs.title: .NET / Razor
docs.text:
rg -n \
'Html\.Raw|WriteLiteral|Response\.Write|@Html\.|IHtmlContent' \
-g '*.cs' \
-g '*.cshtml' \
.

docs.title: PHP
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\becho\b|\bprint\b|\bprintf\s*\(' \
-g '*.php' \
.

These functions are extremely common.

Use them as output discovery, not vulnerability proof.

docs.title: Browser JavaScript
docs.text:
rg -n \
'innerHTML|outerHTML|insertAdjacentHTML|document\.write|document\.writeln' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
-g '*.jsx' \
-g '*.tsx' \
.

Framework-specific dangerous output:

rg -n \
'dangerouslySetInnerHTML|v-html|\[innerHTML\]' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
-g '*.jsx' \
-g '*.tsx' \
-g '*.vue' \
-g '*.html' \
.

docs.title: DOM XSS Sources
docs.text:
rg -n \
'location\.(href|search|hash)|document\.(URL|documentURI|referrer)|window\.name|localStorage|sessionStorage|event\.data|message\.data' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

Combine with sink searches and manually trace flows.

docs.title: postMessage Security
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'addEventListener\(["'\'']message|onmessage|postMessage\(' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

Then inspect origin validation:

rg -n \
'event\.origin|e\.origin|message\.origin' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

Do not assume absence of a nearby origin string proves missing validation. Follow the complete handler.

docs.title: Prototype Pollution
docs.text:
Search object merge and assignment patterns:

rg -n \
'Object\.assign|merge\(|deepMerge|extend\(|set\(|__proto__|constructor\.prototype|prototype\[' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

Prototype pollution requires careful data-flow and object-path analysis.

docs.title: Java / Spring
docs.text:
rg -n \
'redirect:|RedirectView|sendRedirect\(|Location' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET
docs.text:
rg -n \
'Redirect\(|RedirectPermanent\(|RedirectPreserveMethod\(|LocalRedirect\(|Response\.Redirect|Location' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: PHP
docs.text:
rg -n \
'header\s*\(\s*["'\'']Location:|header\s*\(' \
-g '*.php' \
.

docs.title: Django / Flask
docs.text:
rg -n \
'redirect\(|HttpResponseRedirect|HttpResponsePermanentRedirect' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js
docs.text:
rg -n \
'res\.redirect\(|Location' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

docs.title: Browser JavaScript Redirects
docs.text:
rg -n \
'window\.location|location\.href|location\.assign|location\.replace' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

Trace whether attacker-controlled data determines the destination.

docs.title: CSRF Review
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'csrf|xsrf|anti.?forgery|antiforgery|SameSite' \
.

docs.title: Spring Security CSRF
docs.text:
rg -n \
'\.csrf\(|csrf\.disable|ignoringRequestMatchers|CsrfToken' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Do not automatically report:

csrf.disable()

The application may be a stateless API using explicit bearer tokens.

Determine the authentication model.

docs.title: .NET CSRF
docs.text:
rg -n \
'ValidateAntiForgeryToken|AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken|IgnoreAntiforgeryToken|IAntiforgery|Antiforgery' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: Django CSRF
docs.text:
rg -n \
'csrf_exempt|csrf_protect|CsrfViewMiddleware|CSRF_' \
-g '*.py' \
.

csrf_exempt deserves review, but is not automatically vulnerable.

docs.title: Flask CSRF
docs.text:
rg -ni \
'CSRFProtect|csrf\.exempt|WTF_CSRF|csrf' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js CSRF
docs.text:
rg -ni \
'csrf|csurf|SameSite' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

docs.title: CORS Review
docs.text:
General:

rg -ni \
'cors|Access-Control-Allow-Origin|allowedOrigins|allowedOriginPatterns|allowCredentials|credentials' \
.

docs.title: Spring CORS
docs.text:
rg -n \
'@CrossOrigin|CorsConfiguration|allowedOrigins|allowedOriginPatterns|allowCredentials|CorsFilter|WebMvcConfigurer' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET CORS
docs.text:
rg -n \
'AddCors|UseCors|WithOrigins|AllowAnyOrigin|AllowCredentials|AllowAnyHeader|AllowAnyMethod' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: Django CORS
docs.text:
rg -n \
'CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS|CORS_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS|CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS|corsheaders' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Flask CORS
docs.text:
rg -n \
'CORS\(|cross_origin|supports_credentials|origins' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Express CORS
docs.text:
rg -n \
'cors\(|Access-Control-Allow-Origin|credentials\s*:' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

docs.title: Clickjacking and Security Headers
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'X-Frame-Options|frame-ancestors|Content-Security-Policy|Strict-Transport-Security|X-Content-Type-Options|Referrer-Policy|Permissions-Policy' \
.

Missing header configuration in source code does not prove the header is missing in production.

It may be applied by:

Reverse proxy
Web server
CDN
API gateway
Cloud platform

docs.title: Host Header Candidates
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'getServerName|getHeader\(["'\'']Host|Request\.Host|HTTP_HOST|request\.host|req\.hostname|req\.headers\.host|X-Forwarded-Host|Forwarded' \
.

High-value usage includes:

Password reset URL generation
OAuth callbacks
Absolute URLs
Redirects
Email links
Security decisions

docs.title: Proxy Trust
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'trust proxy|ForwardedHeaderFilter|forward-headers|X-Forwarded-For|X-Forwarded-Proto|ProxyFix|ForwardedHeaders' \
.

Proxy trust can influence:

Client IP
Scheme
Host
Secure cookies
Redirect URLs
Rate limiting

docs.title: Session Management
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'session|JSESSIONID|HttpSession|SESSION_COOKIE|express-session|cookie-session|AddSession|UseSession|SameSite|HttpOnly|Secure' \
.

docs.title: Java Sessions
docs.text:
rg -n \
'HttpSession|getSession\(|invalidate\(|changeSessionId|SessionCreationPolicy|sessionManagement' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET Sessions and Cookies
docs.text:
rg -n \
'AddSession|UseSession|HttpContext\.Session|AddCookie|CookieSecurePolicy|HttpOnly|SameSite' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: Django Sessions
docs.text:
rg -n \
'SESSION_COOKIE|SESSION_ENGINE|request\.session|cycle_key\(|flush\(' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Flask Sessions
docs.text:
rg -n \
'SECRET_KEY|session\[|session\.|SESSION_COOKIE|Flask-Session' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Express Sessions
docs.text:
rg -n \
'express-session|cookie-session|req\.session|session\.destroy|regenerate\(' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

docs.title: JWT Review
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'jwt|jsonwebtoken|JwtDecoder|JwtEncoder|NimbusJwtDecoder|AddJwtBearer|decode\(|verify\(|sign\(' \
.

Review:

Signature verification
Issuer
Audience
Expiration
Algorithm selection
Key handling
Custom claims
Authorisation

docs.title: Spring JWT
docs.text:
rg -n \
'JwtDecoder|JwtEncoder|NimbusJwtDecoder|oauth2ResourceServer|JwtAuthenticationConverter|JwtValidators|JwtClaimValidator' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET JWT
docs.text:
rg -n \
'AddJwtBearer|TokenValidationParameters|ValidateIssuer|ValidateAudience|ValidateLifetime|IssuerSigningKey|JwtSecurityTokenHandler' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: Python JWT
docs.text:
rg -n \
'jwt\.decode|jwt\.encode|PyJWT|python-jose|JWT' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js JWT
docs.text:
rg -n \
'jwt\.verify|jwt\.decode|jwt\.sign|jsonwebtoken' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

decode() and verify() are not equivalent operations in many JWT libraries.

Inspect actual security decisions.

docs.title: OAuth / OIDC
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'oauth|oidc|openid|client_secret|client_id|redirect_uri|redirectUri|authorization_code|pkce|code_verifier|nonce|state' \
.

Review:

Redirect URI handling
State
Nonce
PKCE
Token validation
Issuer
Audience
Account linking
Custom callbacks

docs.title: SAML
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'saml|SAMLResponse|SAMLRequest|RelyingParty|Assertion|Metadata|EntityDescriptor' \
.

Review framework configuration and any custom:

Signature handling
Issuer validation
Audience validation
Recipient validation
Replay handling
Account mapping

docs.title: Password Reset
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'forgot.?password|password.?reset|reset.?token|resetPassword|PasswordReset|recovery' \
.

Then trace:

Request
   |
   v
Token Generation
   |
   v
Storage
   |
   v
Email Link
   |
   v
Token Validation
   |
   v
Password Change

Review:

Token entropy
Expiration
Single use
User enumeration
Host handling
Rate limiting
Session invalidation

docs.title: MFA / OTP
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'mfa|2fa|totp|otp|one.?time|authenticator|verification.?code|backup.?code' \
.

Review:

Enrollment
Verification
Recovery
Bypass paths
Rate limiting
Replay
Backup codes
Sensitive-action enforcement

docs.title: Mass Assignment
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'BeanUtils\.copyProperties|ModelMapper|@ModelAttribute|TryUpdateModel|UpdateModel|Object\.assign|req\.body|request\.data' \
.

Look for:

Request Object
     |
     v
Domain / ORM Entity
     |
     v
Database

Sensitive fields include:

role
isAdmin
permissions
ownerId
tenantId
balance
verified
status

docs.title: Race Conditions
docs.text:
Static search can identify concurrency-related controls.

Search:

rg -ni \
'transaction|@Transactional|synchronized|Lock|ReentrantLock|@Version|optimistic|pessimistic|SELECT .* FOR UPDATE|atomic|mutex|semaphore' \
.

Absence of these keywords does not prove a race condition.

The database may enforce atomicity or constraints elsewhere.

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'rate.?limit|throttl|bucket4j|resilience4j|RequestRateLimiter|express-rate-limit|slowapi|limiter|TooManyRequests|429' \
.

Remember:

No rate limiting in application code
    !=
No rate limiting

It may be implemented by:

CDN
WAF
Reverse proxy
API gateway
Load balancer

docs.title: Cache Security
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'@Cacheable|CacheManager|MemoryCache|IMemoryCache|Redis|cache\.get|cache\.set|cached' \
.

Review cache keys for:

User identity
Tenant
Organisation
Role
Permission
Resource

docs.title: Secrets Exposure
docs.text:
General search:

rg --hidden -ni \
-g '!.git/**' \
'password|passwd|secret|api[_-]?key|access[_-]?token|refresh[_-]?token|private[_-]?key|client[_-]?secret' \
.

docs.title: Assignment-Like Secret Patterns
docs.text:
rg --hidden -ni \
-g '!.git/**' \
'(password|passwd|secret|api[_-]?key|access[_-]?token|client[_-]?secret)\s*[:=]' \
.

Expect false positives.

docs.title: Private Keys
docs.text:
rg --hidden -n \
'BEGIN (RSA |EC |OPENSSH |DSA )?PRIVATE KEY' \
-g '!.git/**' \
.

docs.title: Configuration Files
docs.text:
rg --files --hidden \
-g '!.git/**' \
| grep -Ei \
'(^|/)\.env|application.*\.(yml|yaml|properties)|appsettings.*\.json|settings\.py|config|secret|credential|docker|compose|k8s|kubernetes|terraform'

docs.title: GitHub Actions and CI/CD
docs.text:
rg --hidden -ni \
-g '.github/**' \
'secret|token|password|credential|curl|wget|npm|pip|mvn|gradle|docker' \
.

Also inspect:

.gitlab-ci.yml
Jenkinsfile
azure-pipelines.yml
CircleCI
Buildkite

docs.title: Cryptography
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'Cipher|MessageDigest|SecureRandom|Random\(|AES|DES|3DES|RC4|RSA|MD5|SHA1|SHA-1|bcrypt|scrypt|argon|PBKDF|KeyGenerator|SecretKeySpec' \
.

Do not report:

MD5 found

without determining its use.

For example:

MD5 for a non-security cache identifier

has a different security implication from:

MD5 for password storage

docs.title: Java Cryptography
docs.text:
rg -n \
'Cipher\.getInstance|MessageDigest\.getInstance|SecureRandom|new Random\(|SecretKeySpec|KeyGenerator|KeyPairGenerator' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET Cryptography
docs.text:
rg -n \
'MD5|SHA1|SHA256|Aes|DES|TripleDES|RandomNumberGenerator|System\.Random|Rfc2898DeriveBytes|PasswordHasher' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: Python Cryptography
docs.text:
rg -n \
'hashlib|random\.|secrets\.|Crypto\.|cryptography\.|bcrypt|argon2|pbkdf2' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js Cryptography
docs.text:
rg -n \
'crypto\.|Math\.random|bcrypt|argon2|pbkdf2|createHash|createCipher|createCipheriv' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

docs.title: Logging and Sensitive Data
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'logger\.|log\.|Console\.Write|System\.out\.print|console\.log|print\(' \
.

Then search nearby sensitive values.

Examples:

rg -ni \
'log.*(password|token|secret|authorization|cookie)|logger.*(password|token|secret|authorization|cookie)' \
.

Expect false positives.

docs.title: Log Injection / Forging
docs.text:
Identify logging of attacker-controlled:

Headers
Usernames
URLs
Request parameters
User-Agent
Referer

Search sources and logger calls, then trace manually.

docs.title: Error Handling and Information Disclosure
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'stacktrace|printStackTrace|traceback|debug\s*=\s*true|DEBUG\s*=\s*True|UseDeveloperExceptionPage|exception\.message|exception\.stack|console\.error' \
.

Also:

rg -ni \
'debug|development|verbose|stack.?trace|show.?errors' \
.

Configuration and environment matter.

docs.title: Spring Boot Actuator
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'actuator|management\.endpoints|management\.endpoint|management\.server|show-details|health|heapdump|env|configprops|loggers' \
-g '*.properties' \
-g '*.yml' \
-g '*.yaml' \
.

Actuator presence is not automatically information disclosure.

Review:

Exposure
Network accessibility
Authentication
Authorisation
Environment

docs.title: Django Debug Configuration
docs.text:
rg -n \
'DEBUG\s*=|ALLOWED_HOSTS|SECRET_KEY|CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS|SECURE_|SESSION_COOKIE|CSRF_COOKIE' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Flask Debug
docs.text:
rg -n \
'debug\s*=\s*True|DEBUG\s*=|app\.run\(' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Express Security Configuration
docs.text:
rg -n \
'helmet\(|trust proxy|express-session|cookie-session|cors\(|rateLimit|x-powered-by' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

docs.title: Dependency Security
docs.text:
Find manifests:

rg --files | grep -E \
'pom\.xml|build\.gradle|build\.gradle\.kts|package\.json|package-lock\.json|yarn\.lock|pnpm-lock\.yaml|composer\.json|composer\.lock|requirements\.txt|poetry\.lock|Pipfile\.lock|pyproject\.toml|\.csproj$|packages\.lock\.json$'

ripgrep can locate dependencies, but vulnerability determination should use appropriate software composition analysis and version/context review.

docs.title: Java Dependencies
docs.text:
rg -n \
'<dependency>|<groupId>|<artifactId>|<version>' \
-g 'pom.xml' \
.

Gradle:

rg -n \
'implementation|api|compileOnly|runtimeOnly|testImplementation' \
-g 'build.gradle' \
-g 'build.gradle.kts' \
.

docs.title: .NET Dependencies
docs.text:
rg -n \
'PackageReference|PackageVersion|packages\.config' \
-g '*.csproj' \
-g '*.props' \
-g '*.targets' \
-g 'packages.config' \
.

docs.title: PHP Dependencies
docs.text:
rg -n \
'"require"|"require-dev"' \
-g 'composer.json' \
.

docs.title: Python Dependencies
docs.text:
rg -n \
'.+' \
-g 'requirements*.txt' \
-g 'pyproject.toml' \
-g 'Pipfile' \
.

docs.title: Node.js Dependencies
docs.text:
rg -n \
'"dependencies"|"devDependencies"|"peerDependencies"|"optionalDependencies"' \
-g 'package.json' \
.

docs.title: GraphQL Discovery
docs.text:
General:

rg -ni \
'graphql|resolver|mutation|subscription|DataFetcher|QueryMapping|MutationMapping|SubscriptionMapping' \
.

docs.title: Spring GraphQL
docs.text:
rg -n \
'@QueryMapping|@MutationMapping|@SubscriptionMapping|@SchemaMapping|DataFetcher|GraphQlSource' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: Python GraphQL
docs.text:
rg -ni \
'graphene|strawberry|ariadne|resolver|mutation|subscription' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js GraphQL
docs.text:
rg -ni \
'apollo|graphql|resolver|typeDefs|Mutation|Subscription' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

Review resolver-level:

Authentication
Authorisation
Object ownership
Input validation
Rate limiting

docs.title: gRPC Discovery
docs.text:
Find protocol files:

rg --files -g '*.proto'

Search:

rg -n \
'\bservice\b|\brpc\b' \
-g '*.proto' \
.

Java:

rg -n \
'BindableService|ImplBase|StreamObserver|@GrpcService' \
-g '*.java' \
.

.NET:

rg -n \
'Grpc\.Core|BindService|ServerCallContext|MapGrpcService' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

Python:

rg -n \
'grpc\.server|Servicer|add_.*Servicer_to_server' \
-g '*.py' \
.

Node.js:

rg -ni \
'@grpc/grpc-js|grpc\.loadPackageDefinition|addService' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

docs.title: WebSocket Discovery
docs.text:
General:

rg -ni \
'websocket|sockjs|stomp|socket\.io|ws://' \
.

docs.title: Spring WebSocket
docs.text:
rg -n \
'@MessageMapping|WebSocketConfigurer|WebSocketMessageBrokerConfigurer|ChannelInterceptor|StompEndpointRegistry' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET WebSockets / SignalR
docs.text:
rg -n \
'WebSocket|SignalR|Hub\b|MapHub|HubConnection' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: Python WebSockets
docs.text:
rg -ni \
'websocket|websockets|SocketIO|channels|AsyncWebsocketConsumer' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js WebSockets
docs.text:
rg -ni \
'socket\.io|WebSocketServer|new WebSocket|ws\.Server|io\.on' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

Review message-level authorisation, not only connection authentication.

docs.title: Background Jobs
docs.text:
Security review should not stop at HTTP routes.

Search:

rg -ni \
'scheduled|scheduler|cron|background|worker|job|queue|consumer|listener|async' \
.

docs.title: Spring Background Processing
docs.text:
rg -n \
'@Scheduled|@Async|@EventListener|ApplicationListener|CommandLineRunner|ApplicationRunner' \
-g '*.java' \
.

docs.title: .NET Background Processing
docs.text:
rg -n \
'BackgroundService|IHostedService|ExecuteAsync|Task\.Run|Timer' \
-g '*.cs' \
.

docs.title: Python Background Processing
docs.text:
rg -ni \
'celery|@task|@shared_task|rq\.|apscheduler|schedule\.' \
-g '*.py' \
.

docs.title: Node.js Background Processing
docs.text:
rg -ni \
'bullmq|bull|agenda|node-cron|setInterval|worker_threads' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
.

docs.title: Message Queues
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'kafka|rabbitmq|amqp|jms|sqs|servicebus|redis.*queue|consumer|producer|listener' \
.

docs.title: Java Messaging
docs.text:
rg -n \
'@KafkaListener|KafkaTemplate|@RabbitListener|RabbitTemplate|@JmsListener|JmsTemplate' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Messages should be treated according to their actual trust boundary.

An internal queue is not automatically trusted.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'webhook|callback|signature|hmac|event.?type' \
.

Look for:

Signature verification
Replay protection
Timestamp checks
Event validation
Authorisation

docs.title: HTTP Request Smuggling Review
docs.text:
Source code can identify:

Custom HTTP parsing
Transfer-Encoding handling
Content-Length handling
Header normalisation
Proxy assumptions

Search:

rg -ni \
'Content-Length|Transfer-Encoding|chunked|HTTP parser|raw headers' \
.

However:

source code match
    !=
request smuggling vulnerability

The complete HTTP chain must be considered.

docs.title: HTTP Cache Security
docs.text:
Search:

rg -ni \
'Cache-Control|Vary|ETag|Expires|@Cacheable|ResponseCache|cache-control' \
.

Review whether responses containing:

User-specific data
Tenant-specific data
Authenticated data

can become incorrectly shared.

docs.title: Third-Party JavaScript
docs.text:
Search external scripts:

rg -n \
'<script[^>]+src=|https://.*\.js' \
-g '*.html' \
-g '*.htm' \
-g '*.cshtml' \
-g '*.jsp' \
-g '*.php' \
.

Search integrity attributes:

rg -n \
'integrity=|crossorigin=' \
-g '*.html' \
-g '*.htm' \
-g '*.cshtml' \
-g '*.jsp' \
-g '*.php' \
.

Absence of SRI is not automatically a vulnerability.

Review the actual third-party trust model.

docs.title: Source Maps
docs.text:
Find source maps:

rg --files -g '*.map'

References:

rg -n \
'sourceMappingURL' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.css' \
.

Source maps may reveal:

Original source
Internal paths
Comments
Endpoints
Secrets accidentally embedded in client code

Their presence alone does not automatically constitute a vulnerability.

docs.title: Client-Side Secrets
docs.text:
Search browser code:

rg -ni \
'api[_-]?key|secret|token|client[_-]?secret|authorization|bearer' \
-g '*.js' \
-g '*.ts' \
-g '*.jsx' \
-g '*.tsx' \
.

Remember that some public API identifiers are intentionally exposed.

Determine whether the credential grants sensitive capabilities.

docs.title: AI / LLM Integration Discovery
docs.text:
Where an application integrates AI or LLM services, identify the integration points:

rg -ni \
'openai|anthropic|gemini|ollama|langchain|llamaindex|prompt|system.?prompt|tool.?call|function.?call|embedding|vector.?store|rag' \
.

This is primarily attack-surface discovery.

Review:

Prompt construction
Untrusted content
Tool permissions
Output handling
Secrets
RAG sources
External requests
Authorisation

docs.title: Mass Route Search Across Languages
docs.text:
For mixed repositories:

rg -n \
'@RequestMapping|@GetMapping|@PostMapping|\[HttpGet|\[HttpPost|MapGet\(|MapPost\(|@.*\.route\(|\bpath\(|\bre_path\(|\bapp\.(get|post|put|patch|delete)\(|\brouter\.(get|post|put|patch|delete)\(' \
.

Expect noise.

Technology-specific passes are normally better.

docs.title: Broad Source Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'@RequestParam|@PathVariable|@RequestBody|Request\.Query|Request\.Form|\$_GET|\$_POST|request\.GET|request\.POST|request\.args|request\.form|req\.query|req\.params|req\.body' \
.

docs.title: Broad Command Sink Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'Runtime\.getRuntime|ProcessBuilder|Process\.Start|ProcessStartInfo|system\(|shell_exec\(|passthru\(|proc_open\(|os\.system|subprocess\.|child_process|execSync\(' \
.

docs.title: Broad SSRF Sink Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'HttpClient|WebClient|RestTemplate|RestClient|URLConnection|requests\.|httpx\.|urlopen|curl_exec|axios\.|fetch\(|http\.request|https\.request' \
.

docs.title: Broad Deserialisation Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'ObjectInputStream|readObject\(|BinaryFormatter|LosFormatter|NetDataContractSerializer|unserialize\(|pickle\.load|yaml\.load|XMLDecoder|XStream|activateDefaultTyping' \
.

docs.title: Broad XSS Sink Search
docs.text:
rg -n \
'innerHTML|outerHTML|insertAdjacentHTML|document\.write|Html\.Raw|th:utext|dangerouslySetInnerHTML|v-html|Response\.Write' \
.

docs.title: Broad Secret Search
docs.text:
rg --hidden -ni \
-g '!.git/**' \
'password|passwd|secret|api[_-]?key|access[_-]?token|refresh[_-]?token|private[_-]?key|client[_-]?secret' \
.

docs.title: Search Output to Files
docs.text:
Store results:

mkdir -p review/ripgrep

Routes:

rg -n \
'@RequestMapping|@GetMapping|@PostMapping|app\.get|app\.post|\[HttpGet|\[HttpPost' \
. \
> review/ripgrep/routes.txt

Commands:

rg -n \
'ProcessBuilder|Runtime\.getRuntime|Process\.Start|os\.system|subprocess|child_process' \
. \
> review/ripgrep/command-sinks.txt

SSRF:

rg -n \
'HttpClient|WebClient|RestTemplate|requests\.|axios\.|fetch\(' \
. \
> review/ripgrep/ssrf-sinks.txt

docs.title: Useful Output Options
docs.text:
No headings:

rg --no-heading -n 'ProcessBuilder' .

Only matching text:

rg -o 'ProcessBuilder' .

Column numbers:

rg --column -n 'ProcessBuilder' .

JSON output:

rg --json 'ProcessBuilder' .

JSON output can be useful when integrating rg into custom analysis scripts.

docs.title: Search Files Containing a Sink
docs.text:
rg -l \
'ProcessBuilder|Runtime\.getRuntime' \
-g '*.java' \
.

This provides a quick list of high-interest files.

docs.title: Count Dangerous APIs
docs.text:
rg -c \
'ProcessBuilder|Runtime\.getRuntime' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Useful for prioritisation, not vulnerability counting.

docs.title: Search Files Without a Pattern
docs.text:
Sometimes the absence of a security annotation is interesting.

For example, list Java controllers:

rg -l \
'@(RestController|Controller)' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Then manually inspect their authorisation.

Trying to infer "missing authorisation" with regex alone is unreliable because security may be enforced globally.

docs.title: Piping to Other Tools
docs.text:
Example:

rg -l \
'ProcessBuilder|Runtime\.getRuntime' \
-g '*.java' \
. \
| sort -u

Count files:

rg -l \
'ProcessBuilder|Runtime\.getRuntime' \
-g '*.java' \
. \
| wc -l

docs.title: Finding Custom Security Helpers
docs.text:
Search names such as:

rg -ni \
'sanitize|validate|escape|safe|secure|permission|authorize|allowed|trusted' \
.

Interesting functions might include:

validateUrl()
safeExecute()
sanitizeFilename()
checkAccess()
hasPermission()

Open them.

A function called:

safeExecute()

may not actually be safe.

docs.title: Variant Analysis with ripgrep
docs.text:
Suppose manual review confirms a vulnerability in:

CommandRunner.runCommand()

Find every call:

rg -n \
'runCommand\(' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Then search related helpers:

rg -n \
'CommandRunner|runCommand|executeCommand|shellCommand' \
-g '*.java' \
.

This is one of ripgrep's strongest security use cases.

docs.title: Variant Analysis Workflow
docs.text:
Confirmed Vulnerability
        |
        v
Identify Vulnerable Function
        |
        v
rg Function Name
        |
        v
Find Every Caller
        |
        v
Find Similar Functions
        |
        v
Review Each Flow
        |
        v
Identify Variants

docs.title: Turning ripgrep Patterns into SAST Rules
docs.text:
A useful workflow is:

ripgrep
   |
   v
Find Pattern
   |
   v
Manual Validation
   |
   v
Understand Syntax
   |
   +----------------+
   |                |
   v                v
Semgrep          OpenGrep
   |                |
   +-------+--------+
           |
           v
    Reusable Rule

If deeper data-flow analysis is needed:

Confirmed Pattern
       |
       v

docs.title: Example - SQL Injection Review
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'createNativeQuery\(' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Candidate:

String query =
    "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '"
    + username
    + "'";

entityManager.createNativeQuery(query);

Now find where username originates.

VS Code:

Find References
Go to Definition
Call Hierarchy

Possible flow:

@RequestParam username
        |
        v
UserController.search()
        |
        v
UserService.search()
        |
        v
UserRepository.search()
        |
        v
String Concatenation
        |
        v
createNativeQuery()

This is a strong SQL injection candidate.

docs.title: Example - Safe SQL Candidate
docs.text:
Search identifies:

PreparedStatement statement =
    connection.prepareStatement(
        "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ?"
    );

statement.setString(
    1,
    username
);

Result:

Source exists
Sink exists
Parameter binding exists

The search match alone should not be reported.

docs.title: Example - SSRF Review
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'HttpClient' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Candidate:

URI uri =
    URI.create(request.getParameter("url"));

HttpRequest request =
    HttpRequest.newBuilder(uri).build();

client.send(
    request,
    HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString()
);

Flow:

HTTP Parameter
      |
      v
URI.create()
      |
      v
HttpRequest
      |
      v
HttpClient.send()

Now search for validation:

rg -n \
'validateUrl|allowedHost|allowedDomain|allowlist|isAllowed|isPrivate|loopback' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Then inspect:

Scheme
Host
Resolved address
Port
Redirects
Egress

docs.title: Example - Command Execution Review
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'ProcessBuilder' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Candidate:

new ProcessBuilder(
    "/usr/bin/convert",
    inputFile,
    outputFile
).start();

Questions:

Can inputFile contain argument-like values?

Can outputFile alter program behaviour?

Are filenames generated by the server?

Can the executable path be changed?

Is a shell involved?

Does the target program itself interpret special syntax?

Do not simply report:

ProcessBuilder = command injection

docs.title: Example - IDOR Review
docs.text:
Search:

rg -n \
'findById\(' \
-g '*.java' \
.

Candidate:

@GetMapping("/documents/{id}")
public Document get(
    @PathVariable Long id
) {
    return repository
        .findById(id)
        .orElseThrow();
}

Now search the surrounding code for:

Principal
Authentication
SecurityContext
owner
userId
tenant
permission
PreAuthorize

Potential flow:

Attacker-Controlled ID
        |
        v
findById(id)
        |
        v
Document
        |
        v
Response

Missing ownership check may indicate IDOR/BOLA.

docs.title: Example - Stored XSS
docs.text:
Search output sinks:

rg -n \
'th:utext' \
-g '*.html' \
.

Candidate:

<div th:utext="${profile.biography}"></div>

Trace backwards:

profile.biography
       ^
       |
Database
       ^
       |
Profile Update
       ^
       |
HTTP Input

This is a second-order flow:

HTTP Input
    |
    v
Database
    |
    v
HTML Sink

docs.title: Example - Second-Order Command Injection
docs.text:
Search command sinks:

rg -n \
'ProcessBuilder|Runtime\.getRuntime' \
.

Suppose:

ScheduledJob
    |
    v
Database filename
    |
    v
Command execution

Now determine where the filename was originally stored:

File Upload
    |
    v
Database
    |
    v
Scheduled Job
    |
    v
Command Sink

Do not limit source analysis to variables in the same function.

docs.title: Search by Security Boundary
docs.text: A useful approach is searching components independently.
